    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p>The <code>aegov-callout</code> component renders a leading icon, a content area, and two optional trailing regions — a single inline link or a row of action buttons — plus an optional dismiss button.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/callout/callout-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a callout"></p>

    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The callout root is a live region whose role is set automatically from <code>variant</code> — <code>error</code> and <code>warning</code> resolve to <code>role="alert"</code> (assertive, interrupts immediately); <code>default</code>, <code>success</code>, and <code>info</code> resolve to <code>role="status"</code> (polite, announced when the screen reader is idle).</li>
<li>Default variant icons are decorative and marked <code>aria-hidden="true"</code>.</li>
<li>The dismiss button is a real <code><button type="button"></code> with a bilingual <code>aria-label</code> (<code>"Close callout"</code> in English, <code>"إغلاق الإشعار"</code> in Arabic, resolved from the nearest <code>dir="rtl"</code> ancestor), and its icon is <code>aria-hidden="true"</code>.</li>
<li>Invalid slot usage (mutually-exclusive <code>actions</code>/<code>link</code>, or a non-button/link child inside <code>actions</code>) renders a visible, <code>role="alert"</code> error message instead of failing silently — misconfiguration is obvious in development rather than shipping a broken notice.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibility">Developer responsibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Pair the variant with explicit wording — colour alone is not sufficient to convey severity. Users with low vision or colour-blindness rely on the text.</li>
<li>Use <code>variant="error"</code> or <code>variant="warning"</code> only for messages that genuinely warrant an assertive interruption. Reserve <code>default</code>, <code>info</code>, and <code>success</code> for everything else.</li>
<li>If you slot a custom icon via the <code>icon</code> slot, mark it <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> yourself (or give it a meaningful <code>aria-label</code> if it conveys information not present in the text).</li>
<li>Dismissing a callout removes it from the render output via internal state — to control visibility from outside, manage the element directly rather than relying on <code>is-dismissible</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="additional-notes">Additional notes</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>size</code> is responsive-string capable (<code>size="sm md:base xl:lg"</code>), matching the same mechanism used by Badge, Banner, and Accordion.</li>
<li>Unlike <code>aegov-banner</code>'s dismiss button, <code>aegov-callout</code>'s dismiss is immediate — there is no exit animation, and <code>aegovCalloutDismiss</code> fires the instant the button is clicked.</li>
</ul>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-drawer</code> renders a panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, with an optional dimming backdrop behind it. It stays where you declare it — moving out of an ancestor only while open, and only if that ancestor would trap it (see <code>is-portal</code>) — takes its stacking order from a shared overlay manager, traps focus inside while open, and locks body scroll.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/drawer/drawer-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a drawer"></p>

    <h2 id="position">Position</h2>
<p><code>position</code> selects which edge the drawer slides from. <code>right</code> is the default and works well for filters and detail panels; <code>left</code> suits primary navigation; <code>top</code> and <code>bottom</code> suit transient toolbars or mobile action sheets.</p>

    <h2 id="controlling-topbottom-height">Controlling top/bottom height</h2>
<p>Top and bottom drawers have <code>height: auto</code> by default — the panel grows to fit whatever is slotted in, up to <code>100dvh</code>. There is no fixed height per <code>size</code> tier for these two positions. To set a specific height, wrap your content in a <code>div</code> and apply the height there — because that wrapper lives in the light DOM (your own markup), ordinary CSS and Tailwind classes work on it directly.</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>

Slotted text, alignment, and any nested form controls adapt to <code>dir="rtl"</code> automatically. On open, the drawer pins the direction resolved at its declared position as <code>dir</code> on the host (removed again on close), so a local <code><div dir="rtl"></code> wrapper still applies if the drawer has to move out of a trapping ancestor.</p>

                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The panel renders with <code>role="dialog"</code> and <code>aria-modal="true"</code>.</li>
<li>Focus is trapped inside the drawer while it is open — <code>Tab</code> and <code>Shift + Tab</code> cycle through its focusable elements only, including focusable elements inside slotted shadow-DOM components (e.g. <code>aegov-button</code>).</li>
<li>On open, the first focusable element in the panel receives focus. If the panel has no focusable content, the panel itself is focused so assistive technology still announces it.</li>
<li>On close, focus is returned to whatever element opened the drawer.</li>
<li>Body scroll is locked while the drawer is open — reference-counted, so it correctly stays locked if another overlay is also open, and only unlocks once the last one closes.</li>
<li><code>Escape</code> always closes the drawer, per WCAG 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap), even ahead of a cancellable <code>aegovDrawerBeforeClose</code> listener.</li>
<li>The drawer stays where it is declared. Only while it is open, and only if an ancestor would trap its fixed-position layers (a <code>transform</code>, <code>filter</code>, stacking context, or hidden ancestor), it moves out of that ancestor and returns on close (<code>is-portal</code>).</li>
<li>While open, the direction resolved at its declared position is pinned as <code>dir</code> on the host, so slotted content keeps an ancestor's <code>dir="rtl"</code> even after a move. A <code>dir</code> you set on the host yourself is left alone.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Always label the drawer.</strong> Set the <code>label</code> prop to the text of the visible heading inside the panel. Without it, screen readers announce only "dialog". Do not rely on <code>aria-labelledby</code> on the host: the dialog lives in a shadow root and cannot resolve an <code>id</code> in your page.</li>
<li>Drive the drawer through a trigger element's click handler calling <code>show()</code> — this is also what lets the component correctly capture and restore focus to that specific trigger on close.</li>
<li>For navigation drawers, use a <code><nav></code> element inside the panel and ensure every link is keyboard-reachable.</li>
<li>Keep a drawer's primary action reachable — a long list of content should scroll inside the panel rather than pushing its action buttons out of view.</li>
<li>Listen for <code>aegovDrawerBeforeClose</code> and call <code>preventDefault()</code> if the panel contains unsaved changes, to prompt the user before discarding them.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Escape</code></td>
<td>Closes the drawer and returns focus to the trigger element. With overlays stacked (a modal opened from the drawer), only the top one responds to <code>Escape</code> and <code>Tab</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Moves focus to the next focusable element inside the panel, wrapping to the first once past the last.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Moves focus to the previous focusable element inside the panel, wrapping to the last once past the first.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Activates the focused button or control.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-dropdown</code> pairs a trigger with a menu panel that is rendered into a portal at <code>document.body</code> on open, positioned relative to the trigger, and animated in.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/dropdown/dropdown-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a dropdown"></p>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Item</th>
<th>Name</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td><strong>Trigger</strong></td>
<td>The default-slotted element the user interacts with — a button, link, or avatar</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>2</code></td>
<td><strong>Panel</strong></td>
<td>The portaled menu surface — position, alignment, gap, and offset apply here</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td><strong>Menu item</strong></td>
<td>Each focusable child inside <code>dropdown-content</code> — a link, button, or <code><hr></code> separator</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="trigger-type">Trigger type</h2>
<p><code>trigger</code> controls how the dropdown opens. <code>click</code> (default) toggles the dropdown on click and closes it on outside click or <code>Escape</code>. <code>hover</code> opens on pointer-enter after <code>delay-start</code>, and closes on pointer-leave with a 100ms grace period so the cursor can cross the gap between trigger and panel. Both accept <code>Enter</code>/<code>Space</code> on a focused trigger, so keyboard users are never limited to hover-only interaction.</p>

                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The first focusable element inside the trigger slot (e.g. <code>aegov-button</code>) automatically receives <code>aria-haspopup="menu"</code>, <code>aria-expanded</code>, and <code>aria-controls</code> (pointing at the menu's id when open). These attributes are set imperatively so they live on the element assistive technology actually reads, not the wrapper <code><div></code>.</li>
<li>The menu element has <code>role="menu"</code> and <code>aria-labelledby</code> linking back to the trigger wrapper's id (<code>tab-behavior="menu-button"</code> only — <code>disclosure</code> mode uses no menu semantics, since it represents plain navigation links, not commands).</li>
<li>Focusable children inside the menu without an explicit <code>role</code> automatically receive <code>role="menuitem"</code> (menu-button mode only).</li>
<li><code>Escape</code> closes the dropdown and returns focus to the trigger, using <code>preventScroll</code> so the page does not jump if the trigger has scrolled out of view.</li>
<li>Keyboard-triggered opens (<code>Enter</code>/<code>Space</code>, or <code>Arrow Down</code>/<code>Arrow Up</code> on the closed trigger) move focus into the menu; pointer opens leave focus on the trigger, matching the WAI-ARIA menu-button pattern.</li>
<li>Only one dropdown is open at a time — opening another automatically closes the previous one. Nested dropdowns are exempt: opening a child does not close its parent.</li>
<li>The dropdown auto-closes if its trigger scrolls out of the viewport, and re-positions on every scroll and resize.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Place a single focusable element in the default slot — a button, link, or avatar with a role/tabindex. The component does not add tab-stop behaviour to arbitrary non-focusable slotted content.</li>
<li>Provide an accessible name on the trigger — visible text, <code>aria-label</code>, or <code>aria-labelledby</code>. This matters especially for icon-only triggers such as a row-actions kebab button.</li>
<li>Ensure every menu item is keyboard-activatable — links, buttons, or elements with a real <code>tabindex</code>.</li>
<li>For destructive items (delete, cancel, sign out) make the consequence clear in the label text; do not rely on colour alone, and consider a divider (<code><hr></code>) to separate them from routine actions.</li>
<li>Reach for <code>tab-behavior="disclosure"</code> when the dropdown represents a navigation sub-menu (links to other pages) rather than a set of commands — <code>aegov-navbar-item</code> sets this automatically.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Toggles the dropdown when the trigger has focus.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Arrow Down</code></td>
<td>Opens the dropdown (focusing the first item) when the trigger has focus and the menu is closed; moves focus to the next item when the menu is open.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Arrow Up</code></td>
<td>Opens the dropdown (focusing the last item) when the trigger has focus and the menu is closed; moves focus to the previous item when the menu is open.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Home</code></td>
<td>Moves focus to the first menu item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>End</code></td>
<td>Moves focus to the last menu item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>A</code>-<code>Z</code>, <code>0</code>-<code>9</code></td>
<td>Type-ahead: moves focus to the next menu item whose label starts with the typed character(s) (500ms reset between keystrokes).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td><code>menu-button</code> mode: moves focus to the next menu item, wrapping to the first after the last. <code>disclosure</code> mode: moves through the menu's links, closing the menu once focus moves past the last item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td><code>menu-button</code> mode: moves focus to the previous menu item, wrapping to the last after the first. <code>disclosure</code> mode: moves backward through the menu's links, closing the menu once focus moves past the first item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Escape</code></td>
<td>Closes the dropdown and returns focus to the trigger.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="introduction">Introduction</h2>
<p><code>aegov-footer</code> renders a single top-level footer element — the page's <code>contentinfo</code> landmark. Use exactly one per page, placed at the very end of the document, not nested inside <code>main</code> or any other landmark.</p>
<p>Internally it embeds <code>aegov-footer-highlights</code> as its hero row — the same relationship <code>aegov-header</code> has with <code>aegov-header-banner</code> — forwarding the <code>highlights</code> slot straight through to it, along with the <code>entity-contact-*</code> properties in the API Reference below. <code>aegov-footer-highlights</code> can also be used entirely on its own wherever just the hero row is needed.</p>
<p><strong>The <code>highlights</code> slot's start-side card is completely open — put anything you want in it.</strong> The component applies no chrome to this card at all: no background, no shadow, no border, no radius, no padding. Your own wrapper <code>div</code> supplies all of it, so the card can be a newsletter signup (as in the example below), a promotional banner, a set of quick links, or anything else worth surfacing above the fold of the footer.</p>
<p><strong>The government Tawasul contact block is mandatory and fixed.</strong> It renders inside the embedded highlights card on every UAE government site and is identical everywhere — there is no property or slot to remove, hide, or restyle any part of it, including the logo. The entity's own contact number and email, if it has them, go in the same card via <code>entity-contact-number</code> / <code>entity-email</code> (and their <code>-label</code> overrides) — never by editing the fixed card itself.</p>
<p>Below the highlights row, a responsive grid holds the <code>brand</code> slot (logo, description, social links) alongside the author-written link columns. Set <code>app-store-href</code> and/or <code>google-play-href</code> to add a "Download our app" badge block right below the <code>brand</code> slot content, in the same first column — provide either alone, or both; nothing renders unless at least one is set.</p>
<p>The bottom bar carries <code>copyright</code> and <code>legal</code> slots for the "© … All rights reserved" line and legal links (privacy policy, accessibility statement, and similar). The copyright line updates every year — author it yourself; the component does not generate or track the year for you.</p>
<p>Neither <code>aegov-footer</code> nor <code>aegov-footer-highlights</code> emits any custom events.</p>

</div>

    <h2 id="authoring-link-columns">Authoring link columns</h2>
<p>Each footer link column is plain HTML — a title element (any tag; <code>h2</code>–<code>h6</code> recommended) as the group's first child, followed by the rest of the column's content:</p>
<div class="not-prose group relative my-4" data-code-block=""><button type="button" data-copy="" aria-label="Copy code" class="absolute end-2 top-2 z-10 inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md bg-whitely-50/10 px-2.5 py-1.5 text-xs font-medium text-whitely-200 opacity-0 transition-opacity duration-150 hover:bg-whitely-50/20 focus-visible:opacity-100 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-primary-400 group-hover:opacity-100 data-[copied]:text-aegreen-300"><svg class="size-3.5 shrink-0" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 256 256" fill="currentColor"><path d="M216,32H88a8,8,0,0,0-8,8V80H40a8,8,0,0,0-8,8V216a8,8,0,0,0,8,8H168a8,8,0,0,0,8-8V176h40a8,8,0,0,0,8-8V40A8,8,0,0,0,216,32ZM160,208H48V96H160Zm48-48H176V88a8,8,0,0,0-8-8H96V48H208Z"></path></svg><span data-copy-label="">Copy</span></button><pre class="overflow-x-auto rounded-lg bg-aeblack-950 p-4 text-sm text-whitely-200 [scrollbar-width:thin] [scrollbar-color:rgb(255_255_255_/_0.12)_transparent] [&::-webkit-scrollbar]:h-1.5 [&::-webkit-scrollbar-track]:bg-transparent [&::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb]:rounded-full [&::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb]:bg-whitely-50/10 hover:[&::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb]:bg-whitely-50/20 [&_code]:[scrollbar-width:thin] [&_code]:[scrollbar-color:rgb(255_255_255_/_0.12)_transparent] [&_code::-webkit-scrollbar]:h-1.5 [&_code::-webkit-scrollbar-track]:bg-transparent [&_code::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb]:rounded-full [&_code::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb]:bg-whitely-50/10 hover:[&_code::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb]:bg-whitely-50/20"><code class="language-html hljs language-xml" data-lang="html" data-highlighted="true" data-scroll-region="region" tabindex="0" role="region" data-scroll-region-ordinal="1" aria-label="Code example" data-scroll-region-named=""><span class="hljs-tag"><<span class="hljs-name">div</span> <span class="hljs-attr">class</span>=<span class="hljs-string">"aegov-footer__group"</span>></span>

<span class="hljs-tag"></<span class="hljs-name">div</span>></span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>No button, no disclosure markup — nothing beyond <code>.aegov-footer__group</code> for you to write. The component owns the mobile/desktop behaviour entirely: below the <code>sm</code> breakpoint (640px), with the default <code>nav-variant="collapsible"</code>, it synthesizes a button around the title's own content and moves everything after it into an auto-managed panel the button toggles — the first column starts open, the rest closed. At <code>sm</code> and up — and always with <code>nav-variant="flat"</code> — that button is unwrapped again: the title goes back to being exactly the plain element you authored, with no button anywhere in the DOM in that state at all — not hidden, not disabled, never created.</p>
<p>This is deliberate, not incidental: a disclosure control that's merely hidden or neutralised (for example, <code>role="presentation"</code> on a still-focusable button) is not reliably suppressed by assistive technology — WAI-ARIA's Presentational Roles Conflict Resolution rule requires user agents to fall back to native semantics on anything that remains focusable. Only genuinely not having a button in the DOM guarantees the title reads as a plain heading everywhere it isn't interactive.</p>
<p>Add <code>role="list"</code> to your list yourself — the component's CSS removes list markers for layout, which strips the implicit list semantics in some browsers unless <code>role="list"</code> is present. This lives in your own slotted markup, so the component cannot add it for you.</p>
<p>The full example below shows several link columns together, alongside every other slot and property.</p>

    <h2 id="nav-variant">Nav variant</h2>
<p>The <code>nav-variant</code> property controls how link columns behave below the <code>sm</code> breakpoint (640px) — independent of the grid's own 2-to-4-column switch at <code>lg</code>. Both values render identically at <code>sm</code> and above, and neither requires any extra authored markup.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong><code>collapsible</code></strong> (default) — below <code>sm</code>, each column toggles independently via the synthesized button described above; the first column starts open, the rest closed.</li>
<li><strong><code>flat</code></strong> — columns are always expanded, at every screen size. No button is ever synthesized, so there is nothing to toggle.</li>
</ul>
<p>The full example below uses the default <code>collapsible</code> value — resize your viewport below 640px to see the toggle behaviour. Set <code>nav-variant="flat"</code> on the same markup for the always-expanded alternative.</p>

</div>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Renders a single top-level footer element, giving the page its <code>contentinfo</code> landmark.</li>
<li>All link columns are wrapped in one navigation region labelled "Footer navigation" (bilingual), rather than a separate navigation landmark per column, avoiding landmark proliferation.</li>
<li>Column titles are plain, untouched elements whenever they aren't genuinely toggleable — no button exists in the DOM in that state at all, so assistive technology reads exactly what was authored (for example "heading level 2, The Ministry"), never a disclosure control's own role.</li>
<li>Below the <code>sm</code> breakpoint, <code>nav-variant="collapsible"</code> synthesizes a real button with live <code>aria-expanded</code>/<code>aria-controls</code>, toggling the panel's <code>hidden</code> attribute — fully keyboard-operable via native button activation (<code>Enter</code>/<code>Space</code>), with no custom keydown handling.</li>
<li>A dev-mode console warning flags a <code>brand</code>-slot link with no accessible name, since that markup is author-owned.</li>
<li>The "Download our app" badges are plain links with translated, human-readable text ("App Store", "Google Play") — nothing icon-only or unlabeled.</li>
<li>The dismiss/toggle focus ring on every interactive element matches <code>aegov-button</code>'s own focus-visible treatment.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Place <code>aegov-footer</code> at the end of the document, not nested inside <code>main</code> or another landmark — and use exactly one per page.</li>
<li>Author each link column as a plain title element (any tag) followed by its content — no extra markup needed for either <code>nav-variant</code> value.</li>
<li>Add <code>role="list"</code> to each column's list, since the component removes list markers via CSS, which strips implicit list semantics in some browsers.</li>
<li>Give every icon-only <code>brand</code>-slot link an accessible name (<code>aria-label</code>, or a visually-hidden <code>sr-only</code> span).</li>
<li>Do not attempt to hide, restyle, or remove the fixed Tawasul contact block — there is no supported way to do so, and it must stay identical across UAE government sites.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Action</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next focusable element (a link, or a synthesized trigger below <code>sm</code>).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Toggle the focused column's panel, when <code>nav-variant="collapsible"</code> and below <code>sm</code>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>After mount and on every update, the wrapper queries its slotted children for an <code>aegov-label</code> and a supported control (see the "Supported controls" table above). When both are present, the control's host gets its <code>field-id</code> as <code>id</code> and the label's <code>for</code> points at it, so clicking the label focuses the control.</li>
<li>Because <code><label for></code> cannot reach inside a control's shadow root, the wrapper also sets <code>aria-label</code> on the control from the label's text, as a screen reader would read it — content marked <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> (such as a decorative "*") is skipped — and keeps it in sync when the label text changes. An <code>aria-label</code> or <code>aria-labelledby</code> you set on the control yourself is never overwritten.</li>
<li>When the linked control is disabled (by its own <code>is-disabled</code> or an ancestor <code><fieldset disabled></code>), the label is dimmed to match.</li>
<li>The wrapper preserves user-set <code>aria-*</code>/<code>data-*</code> attributes via pass-through, so <code>role="group"</code> plus <code>aria-labelledby</code> can be added when grouping multiple controls.</li>
<li>The wrapper itself has no implicit ARIA role — assistive technology treats it as a plain <code><div></code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Place exactly one <code>aegov-label</code> and one supported control inside each form-field. <code>aegov-checkbox-group</code> and <code>aegov-radio-group</code> never get a label link — name them with their own <code>label</code> property, or <code>aria-labelledby</code> (see "Composing a group" above).</li>
<li>For helper or error text, use the control's <code>hint</code> and <code>error-message</code> (or their slots), or set them (or the <code>hint</code> slot) on the wrapper — they are linked with <code>aria-describedby</code> automatically. A separate paragraph is not linked automatically.</li>
<li>Set <code>is-required</code> on the inner control for real HTML5 validation; add your own visible required-indicator in the label's text, since neither the label nor the wrapper render one automatically.</li>
<li>Do not nest one <code>aegov-form-field</code> inside another; with several controls in one wrapper, only the first is linked and receives the cascade.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<p><code>aegov-form-field</code> introduces no keyboard behaviour of its own. All keyboard interaction is handled by the inner control — refer to that control's own documentation for its keyboard map.</p>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-link</code> renders a single real native <code><a></code> element — no shadow DOM, no wrapper markup. In its default form it's a plain styled inline link; setting any button-style prop switches its class output to match <code>aegov-button</code> exactly, while the tag stays a real anchor throughout.</p>

    <h2 id="text-link">Text link</h2>
<p>With no button-style prop set, <code>aegov-link</code> renders a plain inline link in the system's link colour, nothing else. It inherits its size from the surrounding text, so it drops cleanly into a paragraph, a list item, or a table cell. Setting <code>target="_blank"</code> with no explicit <code>rel</code> automatically adds <code>rel="noopener noreferrer"</code>, and <code>download</code> is forwarded straight through to the native anchor.</p>

                <p><strong>Write link text that describes the destination</strong><br>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Renders a real native <code><a></code> element — keyboard-focusable, recognised by assistive technology as a link, and crawlable by search engines, in both its default and button-styled forms.</li>
<li>When <code>target="_blank"</code> is set with no explicit <code>rel</code>, <code>rel="noopener noreferrer"</code> is added automatically to prevent reverse-tabnabbing.</li>
<li><code>is-disabled</code> sets <code>role="link"</code> explicitly, since a native <code><a></code> with no <code>href</code> silently loses its implicit link role — without this, a disabled link would announce as plain text to a screen reader instead of a (disabled) link.</li>
<li><code>aria-*</code>/<code>data-*</code> pass-through attributes (including <code>aria-label</code> for icon-only links) reach the real anchor directly — <code>aegov-link</code> has no shadow root, so there's no boundary for an accessible name to cross.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Write descriptive link text — avoid "click here" or "read more". The slot content is what a screen reader announces when scanning by link.</li>
<li>For <code>is-icon</code> links, always provide <code>aria-label</code> — the icon alone conveys nothing to assistive technology.</li>
<li>Warn people before <code>target="_blank"</code> opens a new tab — a visually-hidden note inside the link (<code><span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></code>) is announced by assistive technology without changing the visible text.</li>
<li>Maintain at least 4.5:1 text contrast if overriding colour via <code>extra-class</code>.</li>
<li><code>is-bold</code> defaults to <code>true</code> and only affects button-styled links — setting it has no visible effect on the default text-link style, since that path doesn't use it at all.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Moves focus to the link. A disabled link is removed from the tab order entirely.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Moves focus away from the link.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code></td>
<td>Activates the link — navigates, or fires <code>aegovLinkClick</code> for interception.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-modal</code> renders a fixed backdrop and a centred (or top/bottom-docked) dialog, both inside a real shadow root. The component stays where it's declared in markup and takes its z-index from a shared overlay manager; only while open, and only if an ancestor would trap it (a <code>transform</code>, <code>filter</code>, stacking context, or hidden ancestor), does it move out of that ancestor, returning on close.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/modal/modal-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a modal"></p>

    <h2 id="opening-and-closing">Opening and closing</h2>
<p>Control the modal imperatively with <code>show()</code>/<code>close()</code>/<code>toggle()</code> from a trigger's click handler, or declaratively by toggling <code>is-open</code> from your framework's own state. Both paths run the identical open/close sequence — the modal correctly opens even when <code>is-open="true"</code> is present from the very first render, not only on a later change.</p>

    <h2 id="composing-with-form-field">Composing with Form Field</h2>
<p>A modal drops naturally around any other component — here, an <code>aegov-form-field</code> for a short, single-field update. Closing with unsaved changes is one of the clearest cases for listening to <code>aegovModalBeforeClose</code>. Save and Cancel close the modal with <code>close()</code>, which fires the same event, so the example keeps the saved note apart from the draft and only cancels the close while the two differ — Save stores the draft first, Cancel reverts it. The guard covers a backdrop click and <code>close()</code>; <code>Escape</code> always closes the modal without firing it (WCAG 2.1.2).</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>
<p>On open, <code>aegov-modal</code> resolves its direction at its declared position — from the nearest <code>dir</code> ancestor, else <code><html dir></code> — and pins it as <code>dir</code> on the host until it closes. A <code>dir="rtl"</code> on a wrapper therefore still applies even if the modal has to move out of a trapping ancestor. Setting <code>dir="rtl"</code> directly on <code>aegov-modal</code>, as below, also works and is never overwritten.</p>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The dialog renders with <code>role="dialog"</code> and <code>aria-modal="true"</code> — confirmed reaching the real inner dialog element regardless of how the modal was opened.</li>
<li>Focus moves to the first focusable element inside the dialog as soon as it opens — confirmed for both a declarative <code>is-open="true"</code> and an imperative <code>show()</code> call. If the dialog has no focusable children, the dialog container itself receives focus so assistive technology still announces it.</li>
<li><code>Tab</code>/<code>Shift + Tab</code> correctly wrap focus within just the dialog's own focusable elements in both directions, without ever reaching the page behind it.</li>
<li>On close, focus is returned to the exact element that had focus when the dialog opened.</li>
<li>Page scroll is locked while the dialog is open (reference-counted, so a second, nested overlay keeps scroll locked until the last one closes) and correctly released on close.</li>
<li>The modal stays where it is declared. Only while it is open, and only if an ancestor would trap its fixed-position layers (a <code>transform</code>, <code>filter</code>, stacking context, or hidden ancestor), it moves out of that ancestor — to <code>document.body</code> as a last resort — and returns on close. Its z-index comes from a shared overlay manager, so it stacks above the page and above any overlay opened before it.</li>
<li>On open, the direction resolved at its declared position is pinned as <code>dir</code> on the host, so the dialog keeps an ancestor's <code>dir="rtl"</code> even after a move.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Always set the <code>label</code> prop — without it, the component logs a console warning, and screen readers announce only "dialog". Do not rely on <code>aria-labelledby</code> on the host: the dialog lives in a shadow root and cannot resolve an <code>id</code> in your page.</li>
<li>Make the heading state the action plainly, so the name alone conveys it. <code>aria-describedby</code> on the host has the same shadow-root limitation and does not link supporting body text.</li>
<li>Listen for <code>aegovModalBeforeClose</code> and call <code>preventDefault()</code> when the user has unsaved changes, then prompt them in place rather than silently discarding data.</li>
<li>For an RTL dialog, set <code>dir="rtl"</code> on the page, an ancestor, or <code>aegov-modal</code> itself — the modal pins the direction it resolves on open, so any of these is kept.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Activate the focused button or control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next focusable element inside the dialog, wrapping to the first after the last.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the previous focusable element, wrapping to the last after the first.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Escape</code></td>
<td>Close the dialog immediately and return focus to the trigger. With overlays stacked, only the top one responds to <code>Escape</code> and <code>Tab</code>. Escape always closes and does <strong>not</strong> fire the cancellable <code>aegovModalBeforeClose</code> event — confirmed live with a listener that calls <code>preventDefault()</code> on <code>aegovModalBeforeClose</code>, which stops a backdrop click from closing the dialog but has no effect on <code>Escape</code>. Build any "are you sure you want to lose this?" guard around the backdrop-click and programmatic-close paths, not around blocking <code>Escape</code> itself.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-navbar</code> renders a <code><nav></code> landmark wrapping a <code><div role="list"></code>. Each <code>aegov-navbar-item</code> host carries <code>role="listitem"</code> and contains either a real <code><a></code> (when <code>href</code> is set) or a non-link <code><span></code> — both carrying the same visual treatment. An item with a <code>dropdown</code> slot additionally renders a chevron <code><button></code> and hands its entire trigger area over to the slotted <code>aegov-dropdown</code>.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/navbar/navbar-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a navbar"></p>

    <h2 id="items-with-a-sub-menu">Items with a sub-menu</h2>
<p>Place an <code>aegov-dropdown</code> in an item's <code>dropdown</code> slot to add a sub-menu — the item automatically injects a chevron toggle and routes its entire rect as the dropdown's trigger area. Set <code>trigger="hover"</code> on the dropdown to also open it on hover. Clicking the chevron opens or closes the menu. From the keyboard, <code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code> or <code>ArrowDown</code> on the focused chevron opens the menu and moves focus to its first item, and <code>Escape</code> closes it. The dropdown is set to <code>tab-behavior="disclosure"</code> automatically, so <code>Tab</code> moves through its links. An item with both an <code>href</code> and a <code>dropdown</code> is intentional — the link navigates, and the chevron independently toggles the menu.</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>
<p>The navbar reads <code>dir="rtl"</code> from the closest <code>[dir]</code> ancestor, or the document root. In RTL mode, <code>ArrowLeft</code> and <code>ArrowRight</code> swap roles so that <code>ArrowLeft</code> moves to the next item, following the reading direction. Sub-menu content is portalled to <code>document.body</code> and copies the resolved direction, so a local <code>dir="rtl"</code> wrapper is enough. Layout, item gaps, and the active-item indicator all mirror automatically, since the underlying flex layout follows the container's text direction.</p>

                <p><strong>Mark exactly one item as the current page</strong><br>
Set <code>is-active</code> on the single item matching the current route. It's the only thing that sets <code>aria-current="page"</code> on the inner link — the one unambiguous "you are here" signal for both sighted and screen-reader users.</p>

                <section class="article-section">
                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Renders as a <code><nav></code> landmark with a configurable <code>aria-label</code>, via <code>label-nav</code>, defaulting to "Main navigation" (English) or "التنقل الرئيسي" (Arabic) when left unset.</li>
<li>Items are exposed as a list — the inner container is a <code><div role="list"></code> and each <code>aegov-navbar-item</code> host carries <code>role="listitem"</code> — so the list structure and item count reach assistive technology. (A native <code><ul></code> is not used because it may not contain the custom-element hosts.)</li>
<li>The active item sets <code>aria-current="page"</code> on its inner link.</li>
<li>A disabled item renders a non-focusable <code><span></code> with <code>aria-disabled="true"</code>, so it is skipped by both <code>Tab</code> and arrow-key navigation. Screen-reader users still encounter it (and its disabled state) when reading through the list.</li>
<li>Arrow-key navigation among items and chevrons via <code>ArrowLeft</code>/<code>ArrowRight</code>/<code>Home</code>/<code>End</code>, wrapping from the last item back to the first — direction-aware in RTL, so <code>ArrowLeft</code> moves to the next item when the reading direction is right-to-left.</li>
<li>When an item has a dropdown, the injected chevron is a real <code><button></code> with an <code>aria-label</code> naming what it controls ("Open Services submenu", or the Arabic equivalent in RTL), and its <code>aria-expanded</code> stays in sync with the dropdown's open state. The dropdown is switched to <code>tab-behavior="disclosure"</code> automatically, since its contents are navigation links rather than a menu of commands.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Mark exactly one item per route with <code>is-active</code>.</li>
<li>Provide a meaningful <code>label-nav</code> whenever a page has more than one navigation landmark — for example, a primary navbar plus a footer navbar.</li>
<li>Keep item labels short — long labels can break the horizontal layout on smaller viewports.</li>
<li>When supplying an icon via <code>icon-start</code>, mark it <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> so the item's label remains the single accessible name.</li>
<li>For dropdown sub-menus, follow <code>aegov-dropdown</code>'s own accessibility guidance for the menu content itself.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Action</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus into and out of the navbar, stopping at each linked item and chevron in turn. Disabled items are skipped.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowRight</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next item or chevron, wrapping to the first. In RTL, moves to the previous one instead.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowLeft</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the previous item or chevron, wrapping to the last. In RTL, moves to the next one instead.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Home</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the first focusable item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>End</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the last focusable item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code></td>
<td>Activate the focused link, or open/close the focused chevron's sub-menu (opening moves focus to its first item).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Space</code></td>
<td>Open/close the focused chevron's sub-menu (opening moves focus to its first item).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowDown</code> (chevron focused)</td>
<td>Open the sub-menu and move focus into it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Escape</code></td>
<td>Close the open sub-menu.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<h3 id="notes-2">Notes</h3>
<ul>
<li>An unknown <code>size</code> token silently falls back to <code>base</code> — no console warning is emitted.</li>
<li>An item with both an <code>href</code> and a <code>dropdown</code> is intentional: the link navigates, and the chevron independently toggles the menu.</li>
<li><code>aegov-navbar-item</code> must be used inside <code><aegov-navbar></code> — using it standalone throws a runtime error during initialisation.</li>
<li>The direction used for arrow keys and the default <code>label-nav</code> is read from the closest <code>[dir]</code> ancestor, falling back to <code><html dir></code>. Sub-menu content is portalled to <code>document.body</code>, but it copies the navbar item's resolved direction, so a local <code>dir="rtl"</code> wrapper works as well as <code>dir</code> on <code><html></code>.</li>
</ul>

</div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-navblock</code> renders a <code><nav></code> landmark with an optional <code><h2></code> title, wrapping a <code><div role="list"></code> of <code>aegov-navblock-item</code> children. Each item host carries <code>role="listitem"</code> and contains a row — a real <code><a></code> (leaf with a destination), a toggle <code><button></code> (parent with sub-items), or a plain <code><button></code>/non-interactive <code><span></code> otherwise — plus, for a parent row, a collapsible <code><div></code> wrapper holding its own nested <code><div role="list"></code> of sub-items.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/navblock/navblock-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a navblock"></p>

    <h2 id="navblock-basics">Navblock basics</h2>
<p>A navblock is one or more <code>aegov-navblock-item</code> children. An item with <code>href</code> and no children renders as a link; an item with nested <code>aegov-navblock-item</code> children automatically becomes a collapsible group — authors do not need to add <code>slot="subnav"</code> themselves, nested items are promoted into it automatically.</p>

    <h2 id="collapsible-and-flat-variants">Collapsible and flat variants</h2>
<p><code>variant</code> switches the visual mode of the whole tree from a single prop on <code>aegov-navblock</code> — the markup underneath is identical either way. <code>collapsible</code> (default) shows nested items in an animated accordion, with the active item getting a filled background highlight. <code>flat</code> renders every item at the same indentation level; items with children become non-interactive bold group headers whose children are always visible, and the active item gets a colour/weight change with no background fill.</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>
<p>The navblock reads <code>dir="rtl"</code> from the closest ancestor carrying a <code>dir</code> attribute (or the document root if none is set) — the same mechanism used across this design system's other navigation components. The sub-list's connector border, indentation, and active-border segment all mirror automatically through CSS logical properties, and the default <code>label-nav</code> switches to Arabic. Keyboard behaviour does not change with direction: <code>ArrowRight</code> always expands and <code>ArrowLeft</code> always collapses a parent row, and <code>ArrowUp</code>/<code>ArrowDown</code> move between rows.</p>

                <p><strong>Mark exactly one item as the current page</strong><br>
Set <code>is-active</code> on the single item matching the current route. If it's nested, its ancestor groups are opened automatically on load so the active row is visible without any extra code.</p>

                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Renders as a <code><nav></code> landmark with a configurable <code>aria-label</code> via <code>label-nav</code>, defaulting to "Sidebar navigation" (English) or "التنقل في الشريط الجانبي" (Arabic) when left unset.</li>
<li>Items are exposed as a list — the inner container and every sub-region are <code><div role="list"></code>, and each <code>aegov-navblock-item</code> host carries <code>role="listitem"</code>. (Native <code><ul></code>/<code><li></code> are not used because a list may not contain the custom-element hosts.)</li>
<li>Parent rows are real <code><button></code> elements with <code>aria-expanded</code> and <code>aria-controls</code> linking the trigger to its sub-region, which is labelled by the trigger (<code>aria-labelledby</code>). A collapsed sub-region is hidden, so its rows are not reachable by <code>Tab</code>.</li>
<li>Leaf rows are <code><a></code> elements when <code>href</code> is set, or <code><button></code> otherwise. The active leaf carries <code>aria-current="page"</code>.</li>
<li>Disabled items are excluded from both <code>Tab</code> and arrow-key navigation: a disabled parent row is a natively <code>disabled</code> <code><button></code>, and a disabled leaf renders as a non-focusable <code><span aria-disabled="true"></code>.</li>
<li>When any descendant item is <code>is-active</code>, every ancestor group is expanded automatically on the initial render, so the active row is never hidden inside a collapsed parent by default.</li>
<li>In <code>variant="flat"</code>, a group header with children renders as a non-interactive <code><span role="presentation"></code> rather than a button, since its children are always visible and there is nothing to toggle.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Mark exactly one item per route with <code>is-active</code>.</li>
<li>Don't set <code>icon</code>, <code>size</code>, or <code>variant</code> directly on an <code>aegov-navblock-item</code> — they cascade from the parent <code>aegov-navblock</code> on every render and a manual value is overwritten on the next update.</li>
<li>Keep a consistent <code>icon</code>/<code>variant</code> choice for a given navblock instance — switching either only visually intended at the whole-tree level.</li>
<li>Provide a meaningful <code>label-nav</code> whenever a page has more than one navigation landmark (for example, a navblock sidebar alongside a header navbar).</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Action</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next visible row. Every link and parent row is its own Tab stop; rows inside a collapsed group and disabled rows are skipped.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowDown</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next visible row, wrapping to the first.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowUp</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the previous visible row, wrapping to the last.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Home</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the first visible row.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>End</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the last visible row.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowRight</code></td>
<td>Expand a closed parent row (focus stays on it). Not swapped in RTL.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowLeft</code></td>
<td>Collapse an open parent row; on a leaf or a closed row, move focus to its parent row instead. Not swapped in RTL.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code></td>
<td>Follow a leaf link, or toggle a parent row open/closed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Space</code></td>
<td>Toggle a parent row open/closed (or activate a leaf rendered as a <code><button></code>).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<h3 id="notes-2">Notes</h3>
<ul>
<li>A group with children rendered in <code>variant="flat"</code> is always visible — its children are never hidden, and its header is not part of arrow-key navigation (there is nothing to toggle).</li>
<li>An unrecognised <code>icon</code> renders the default chevron. An unrecognised <code>variant</code> is not corrected: anything other than <code>flat</code> behaves as <code>collapsible</code>. Both log a console warning in development builds only. An unrecognised <code>size</code> token falls back to <code>base</code> silently.</li>
<li><code>active-border</code> only has a visible effect when <code>variant="flat"</code>; it is otherwise a no-op.</li>
</ul>

</div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-progress</code> renders a custom visual track (and, optionally, a top or trailing counter and a description line) alongside a hidden native <code><progress></code> element carrying the same <code>value</code>/<code>max</code> — the native element exists purely so assistive technology gets correct semantics; the visual track is marked <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> so it isn't announced twice.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/progress/progress-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a progress bar"></p>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Item</th>
<th>Name</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td><strong>Track</strong></td>
<td>The visible background bar, <code>aria-hidden</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>2</code></td>
<td><strong>Fill</strong></td>
<td>The coloured portion, width driven by <code>value</code>/<code>max</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td><strong>Counter</strong></td>
<td>Optional numeric readout — <code>top</code> or <code>trailing</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>4</code></td>
<td><strong>Description</strong></td>
<td>Optional status line below the bar</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>5</code></td>
<td><strong>Native <code><progress></code></strong></td>
<td>Visually hidden; carries the real accessible value</td>

<p>Set <code>value</code> for a determinate bar, or omit it entirely for an indeterminate (loading) state. Always provide a <code>label</code>, an <code>aria-label</code>, or a paired <code><label></code> so screen readers know what the progress represents.</p>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>A hidden native <code><progress></code> element, carrying the same <code>value</code>/<code>max</code>, is always rendered so assistive technology gets correct progress semantics — the visible custom track is <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> so it isn't announced as a duplicate.</li>
<li>When <code>value</code> is omitted, the native <code><progress></code> renders with no <code>value</code> attribute at all, which is what puts it into the browser's own indeterminate state (not a class or ARIA attribute the component invents).</li>
<li>Setting <code>description</code> gives the resulting <code><p></code> an auto-generated <code>id</code> and links it to the native <code><progress></code> via <code>aria-describedby</code> — a developer-supplied <code>aria-describedby</code> pass-through is composed with it, so both are announced.</li>
<li>A console warning fires in development if the bar has no <code>label</code> prop, no <code>aria-label</code>/<code>aria-labelledby</code> pass-through, and no external <code><label for="field-id"></code> pointing at it.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Provide a label via the <code>label</code> prop, <code>aria-label</code>/<code>aria-labelledby</code>, or a real <code><label></code> (typically via <code>aegov-label</code> inside <code>aegov-form-field</code>).</li>
<li>Move from indeterminate to a determinate <code>value</code> as soon as a real completion percentage is known.</li>
<li>Use <code>description</code>, or a sibling <code>aria-live="polite"</code> element, to announce state changes such as "Upload complete".</li>
<li>When <code>counter-suffix</code> is set and the bar is determinate, the component already sets a matching <code>aria-valuetext</code> automatically (e.g. <code>"75%"</code>) — only pass through <code>aria-valuetext</code> manually when you need a fuller custom description (e.g. <code>"6 of 8 documents uploaded"</code>).</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="notes-2">Notes</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>counter-suffix</code> is appended with no automatic spacing — include any leading space or unit yourself (e.g. <code>" MB"</code>).</li>
<li><code>height</code> accepts a Tailwind spacing-scale string; a non-numeric value falls back to the default <code>0.5rem</code> (and logs a console warning).</li>
<li>There are no colour variants (success/error/etc.) by design — communicate status through <code>description</code> or a sibling <code>aegov-callout</code> rather than recolouring the fill.</li>
</ul>

</div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-range</code> renders one real native <code><input type="range"></code> in single mode, or two (low/high) in range mode — visually hidden but focusable and fully keyboard-driven. A custom track, fill, and one or two thumb elements are drawn on top purely for consistent cross-browser visuals; dragging a custom thumb keeps the underlying native input's value in sync.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/range/range-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a range"></p>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Item</th>
<th>Name</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td><strong>Track</strong></td>
<td>The full-width background bar representing <code>min</code> to <code>max</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>2</code></td>
<td><strong>Fill</strong></td>
<td>The coloured segment between the start and the current value (or between the two thumbs in range mode)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td><strong>Thumb</strong></td>
<td>The draggable handle — one in single mode, two (low/high) in range mode</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>4</code></td>
<td><strong>Value display</strong> <em>(optional)</em></td>
<td>Tooltip, in-thumb text, or flanking min/max labels, depending on <code>display</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>5</code></td>
<td><strong>Label</strong></td>
<td>Text naming the field (<code>label</code> prop)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>6</code></td>
<td><strong>Hint / error message</strong></td>
<td>Supporting helper text, which stays visible when the error message appears above it once <code>is-invalid</code> is set</td>
</tr>
</tbody>

    <h2 id="validation">Validation</h2>
<p><code>is-invalid</code> and <code>error-message</code> apply to every native input the slider renders (both thumbs, in range mode). <code>is-required</code> has no validation effect, because a range always has a value — business rules are the realistic case. A common pattern is a group of business rules checked on <code>aegovValidate</code> — for example, enforcing a minimum span between the two thumbs — using <code>setCustomValidity()</code> to surface a message when the rule fails.</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>
<p>The range is direction-agnostic. When the document or any ancestor is <code>dir="rtl"</code>, the fill, the min/max labels, and pointer-to-value mapping all mirror automatically — <code>min</code> sits on the right, <code>max</code> on the left, and dragging toward the start of the track (now the right edge) decreases the value. Arrow keys follow the visual direction as well: <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> increases the value and <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> decreases it. No extra configuration is needed.</p>

    <p>Here is the recommended usage of a range on any website or application. These are recommended usage guides, however the developer must use the best practices of web and application development to accurately use this component.</p>

                <p><strong>Always pair a slider with a visible value, unless the exact number truly doesn't matter</strong><br>
Set <code>display="tooltip"</code>, <code>"thumb"</code>, or <code>"full"</code> so users get feedback on the number they're choosing, not just its relative position on the track.</p>

                <p><strong>Use range mode for a genuine "between X and Y" span, not two independent values</strong><br>
A dual-thumb slider communicates "pick a range" — for two unrelated single numbers (e.g. minimum salary and years of experience), use two separate single-mode sliders or numeric inputs instead.</p>

    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>aegov-range</code> is built on one or two real <code><input type="range"></code> elements, so screen readers, the OS accessibility rotor, and keyboard handling all treat it as a native slider — nothing is reimplemented in ARIA-only markup.</li>
<li><code>aria-valuemin</code>, <code>aria-valuemax</code>, and <code>aria-valuenow</code> are kept in sync as the user drags or types. In range mode, the low thumb's <code>aria-valuemax</code> is clamped to the current high value (and the high thumb's <code>aria-valuemin</code> to the current low value), so each handle always reports its own currently-permitted range.</li>
<li>The custom thumb-and-track visuals sit on top of the real native input(s) purely for consistent cross-browser styling — the native input drives all keyboard interaction, and pointer/touch dragging on the custom thumb keeps the native input's value in sync via re-render, so both interaction paths end up in the same state.</li>
<li>Each thumb in range mode gets a bilingual, self-composed <code>aria-label</code> combining the field's <code>label</code> with the thumb's role — e.g. "Age of dependants — Range minimum" in English, or the Arabic equivalent when the component resolves the document as RTL. No developer translation work is needed.</li>
<li>Hint and error text are wired to every native input the component renders via <code>aria-describedby</code> automatically. The hint stays visible while an error shows, so the description reads the error, then the hint. The error region only takes <code>role="alert"</code> after the user has blurred at least once, so a validation message present at initial load isn't announced as an interruption.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibility">Developer responsibility</h3>
<p>The following is required for a developer to add additionally or pay attention to regarding this component.</p>
<ul>
<li>Always provide a <code>label</code> that names the unit being chosen (km, AED, years) — a bare slider gives users no way to interpret the number.</li>
<li>Pair a slider with a visible numeric readout whenever precision matters — set <code>display</code> to <code>tooltip</code>, <code>thumb</code>, or <code>full</code> rather than leaving it at <code>none</code>.</li>
<li>Keep the value range realistic for a slider. When a user needs to type an exact, arbitrary number, pair with (or use instead) a numeric <code>aegov-input</code>.</li>
<li>In range mode, seed <code>value-low</code>/<code>value-high</code> so that <code>value-low + step ≤ value-high</code> — the component clamps this on every interaction, but a seeded starting value that already violates it is not corrected automatically.</li>
<li>In <code>vertical</code> orientation, the track is <code>200px</code> tall by default — set <code>--range-height</code> on the host or an ancestor when you need a different length.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="additional-notes">Additional notes</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>size</code> accepts a responsive breakpoint string, the same convention used by Badge, Banner, and Checkbox (e.g. <code>size="sm md:base"</code>).</li>
<li>The off-track and the thumb body never change colour with <code>variant</code> — only the active fill segment, the in-thumb value text and the focus ring do. This is a deliberate constant, not a limitation, so the grip stays equally visible across every colour family.</li>
<li><code>name</code>/form submission is handled via <code>ElementInternals</code> on the host element. In range mode this submits two separate <code>FormData</code> entries, <code>{name}-low</code> and <code>{name}-high</code>, rather than one combined value.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Tab</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus to the slider (or, in range mode, to the low thumb, then the high thumb as a separate stop).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus to the previous focusable element.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd></td>
<td>Increases the focused thumb's value by one <code>step</code>. In RTL, Left and Right follow the visual direction, so <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> increases and <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> decreases.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd></td>
<td>Decreases the focused thumb's value by one <code>step</code> (reversed for Left and Right in RTL, as above).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Home</kbd></td>
<td>Jumps the focused thumb to its minimum (<code>min</code> for a single thumb or the low thumb; the low thumb's current value, plus one step, for the high thumb).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>End</kbd></td>
<td>Jumps the focused thumb to its maximum (<code>max</code> for a single thumb or the high thumb; the high thumb's current value, minus one step, for the low thumb).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd></td>
<td>Moves the value by a larger, browser-defined increment.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<p>In range mode, the low and high thumbs are always reachable and adjustable independently via keyboard, exactly as with mouse or touch — a fully-clamped, native-slider-driven interaction where each thumb is its own tab stop.</p>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-select</code> renders in one of two ways depending on <code>appearance</code> (and is forced into the second whenever <code>is-multiple</code> is set): a real native <code><select></code> built from parsed option data, or a custom trigger button plus an absolutely-positioned dropdown panel. Either way, the actual <code><aegov-select-option></code>/<code><aegov-select-option-group></code> children you author are never rendered visibly themselves — they're a declarative data source, parsed once into the options that drive whichever UI is showing.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/select/select-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a select"></p>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>

</tr>
</thead>

<td><strong>Trigger</strong></td>
<td>The native <code><select></code>, or the custom button showing the current value/placeholder (listbox appearance)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>2</code></td>

<tr>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td><strong>Search input</strong> <em>(optional, listbox only)</em></td>
<td>Filters the option list as the user types</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td><strong>Option</strong></td>

    <h2 id="basics">Basics</h2>
<p>The default <code>appearance="default"</code> renders a real native <code><select></code> — the right choice whenever you don't need search or multi-select, since it's the lightest option and gives the best experience on mobile (the OS renders its own picker). Declare each choice as an <code>aegov-select-option</code> child. Always give the select a visible label — every example on this page wraps it in <code>aegov-form-field</code> with an <code>aegov-label</code>.</p>
