                <section class="article-section">
                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The select takes its accessible name from the label around or pointing at it — <code>aegov-form-field</code> + <code>aegov-label</code>, <code><aegov-label for></code>, <code>aria-labelledby</code> or <code>aria-label</code> on the select — and passes it to the real control inside its shadow root, in both appearances; changes to the label text are followed.</li>
<li>The default appearance renders a real native <code><select></code>, so it inherits all native keyboard support, OS-level pickers on mobile, and screen-reader announcements for free — nothing is reimplemented.</li>
<li>The listbox appearance follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern: the trigger has <code>role="combobox"</code>, <code>aria-haspopup="listbox"</code>, <code>aria-expanded</code>, and <code>aria-controls</code> pointing at the panel; the panel has <code>role="listbox"</code>; each option has <code>role="option"</code> and <code>aria-selected</code>; and <code>aria-activedescendant</code> on the trigger tracks the focused option.</li>
<li>Grouped options use <code>role="group"</code> named with <code>aria-label</code> from the group's <code>label</code>; the visible header is hidden from assistive technology so it isn't read twice. In the default appearance, groups render as real <code><optgroup></code> elements.</li>
<li>When <code>is-searchable</code>, the search input itself also declares <code>role="combobox"</code> with its own <code>aria-controls</code>/<code>aria-activedescendant</code>, since focus moves into it while the dropdown is open.</li>
<li>A search that matches nothing is announced through a <code>role="status"</code> region.</li>
<li>The search input's placeholder/label, the clear button's <code>aria-label</code> and the multi-select count ("3 selected" / "تم اختيار 3") are bilingual (English/Arabic, resolved from the document's direction) — no developer translation needed.</li>
<li>The error region only takes <code>role="alert"</code> once the user has genuinely blurred the whole component (focus leaving it entirely, not just moving from the trigger into the search input or an option), <code>validate('submit')</code> has run, or a form validity check has found the field invalid, so a validation message present at initial load isn't announced as an interruption.</li>
<li>A disabled <code>aegov-select-option</code> remains visible (greyed out) but is skipped entirely during keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Home/End, typeahead) and cannot be clicked.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibility">Developer responsibility</h3>
<p>The following is required for a developer to add additionally or pay attention to regarding this component.</p>
<ul>
<li>Give every select a visible label: wrap it in <code>aegov-form-field</code> with an <code>aegov-label</code> (as in every example on this page), or point a standalone <code><aegov-label for="<field-id>"></code> at it, or use <code>aria-labelledby</code> on the select. A <code>placeholder</code> is not a label — it is only shown while nothing is selected, is exposed as the value rather than the name, and disappears once a choice is made (and in multiple mode).</li>
<li>Prefer the default (native) appearance whenever search and multi-select aren't needed — it's lighter, faster, and gives the best experience on mobile, where the OS renders its own picker.</li>
<li>For long lists (countries, services, time slots), set <code>is-searchable="true"</code> so keyboard and screen-reader users can filter instead of scanning every option.</li>
<li><code><aegov-select-option></code> <strong>must</strong> be a descendant of <code><aegov-select></code> (directly, or nested inside an <code><aegov-select-option-group></code>) — using it standalone throws an error at load time, by design, since its only job is to describe one entry in a specific parent select's option list.</li>
<li>Keep option labels reasonably short — the trigger truncates a long single-select label, and multi-select always collapses to a count ("3 selected") rather than listing every choice.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="additional-notes">Additional notes</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>size</code> accepts a responsive breakpoint string, the same convention used by Badge, Banner, and Checkbox (e.g. <code>size="sm md:base"</code>).</li>
<li>Setting <code>is-multiple="true"</code> forces listbox rendering even if <code>appearance="default"</code> is also set (or omitted) — there is no native multi-select UI in this design system.</li>
<li><code>name</code>/form submission is handled differently per appearance: in native mode the real <code><select name></code> submits directly (mirrored onto <code>ElementInternals</code> too, since the native element lives inside a shadow root and wouldn't otherwise be seen by a <code>FormData</code> read); in listbox mode it's entirely <code>ElementInternals</code>-driven, and multi-select submits <strong>one <code>FormData</code> entry per selected value</strong>, not one comma-joined string.</li>
<li>The raw <code><aegov-select-option></code>/<code><aegov-select-option-group></code> children are never rendered visibly themselves — they're a declarative data source only, parsed once into an internal option list that drives the real <code><option></code> elements (native mode) or <code><div role="option"></code> elements (listbox mode).</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support-listbox-appearance">Keyboard support (listbox appearance)</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd></td>
<td>Opens the dropdown when closed, giving visual focus to the currently-selected option (or the first enabled option if none is selected). <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> on a closed select open it on the first/last enabled option.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd></td>
<td>While open, moves focus to the next/previous enabled option.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd></td>
<td>Jumps focus to the first/last enabled option (inside the search input they move the text caret instead).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus 10 enabled options up/down.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd></td>
<td>Selects the focused option. In single-select mode this also closes the dropdown; in multi-select it stays open so more options can be picked.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Escape</kbd></td>
<td>Closes the dropdown without changing the selection and returns focus to the trigger. Only the dropdown closes, not a surrounding modal or drawer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd></td>
<td>In single-select, selects the focused option and closes the dropdown; in multi-select, just closes it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Typing a character</td>
<td>When <code>is-searchable</code> is off, jumps focus to the next enabled option whose label starts with what's been typed (a short-lived buffer, cleared after ~500ms of inactivity) — it moves focus, it does not hide non-matching options. When <code>is-searchable</code> is on, focus is already in the search input on open, and typing there filters the option list instead. Typing on a closed select opens it first.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Tab</kbd></td>
<td>In single-select, selects the focused option; then closes the dropdown and moves focus to the next focusable element (does not cycle inside the panel).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<p>Keyboard support for the default (native) appearance is provided entirely by the browser's own <code><select></code> implementation.</p>

</div>

                <section class="article-section">
                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>With no label, <code>aegov-separator</code> renders a real native <code><hr></code> — inherently correct semantics with zero ARIA needed for the plain case.</li>
<li>Defaults to <code>role="presentation"</code> (<code>is-decorative</code> defaults to <code>true</code>), so a purely visual divider generates no noise for screen readers.</li>
<li>Setting <code>is-decorative="false"</code> exposes <code>role="separator"</code> instead, so assistive technology announces it as a real structural divider.</li>
<li><code>aria-orientation</code> is set to match <code>orientation</code>, but <strong>only</strong> when the separator's role is <code>separator</code> — it's correctly omitted entirely when the role is <code>presentation</code>, since <code>aria-orientation</code> isn't meaningful on an element assistive technology is told to ignore.</li>
<li>Supplying <code>text</code> (or slotted content) always forces <code>role="separator"</code>, even if <code>is-decorative</code> is left at its default <code>true</code> — a labelled divider inherently carries structural meaning, so the component doesn't let it stay purely decorative by accident.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibility">Developer responsibility</h3>
<p>The following is required for a developer to add additionally or pay attention to regarding this component.</p>
<ul>
<li>Use the default decorative mode for purely visual breaks. Only set <code>is-decorative="false"</code> when the divider itself carries meaning worth announcing — for example, separating two distinct groups within a list of results.</li>
<li>A vertical separator needs a height context — place it inside a parent with a defined height (e.g. a flex row with a fixed height) or give the host a height class (e.g. <code>class="h-6"</code>). On its own it only reaches its 1rem minimum height. A height in <code>extra-class</code> has no effect.</li>
<li>Set props in markup before the separator renders. The label check reads the host's children on every render, and an unlabelled separator's own rendered <code><hr></code> counts as one, so changing a prop later switches it to the labelled layout with an empty label. To change an unlabelled separator at runtime, replace the element.</li>
<li>Do not rely on a label being announced — screen readers treat the content of a <code>separator</code> as presentational. Convey the meaning in surrounding text or headings, and mark an icon used as a label <code>aria-hidden="true"</code>.</li>
<li>Keep label text short — a long label in a text-bearing separator can wrap awkwardly on narrow viewports.</li>
</ul>

</div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-tabs</code> is a composite of three elements: the parent container, the trigger (<code>aegov-tab</code>), and the content panel (<code>aegov-tab-panel</code>). The parent writes shared configuration — variant, size, orientation, and which tab is active — onto its children, so individual tabs and panels rarely need any prop beyond their own <code>tab-id</code>.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/tabs/tabs-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of tabs"></p>

    <p>Here is the recommended usage of tabs on any website or application. These are recommended usage guides, however the developer must use the best practices of web and application development to accurately use this component.</p>

</div>

                <p><strong>Use tabs for related views of the same object, not for sequential steps</strong><br>
Tabs imply the user can jump between panels in any order and come back — for a fixed, ordered sequence (like a multi-step form), a stepper or wizard pattern communicates the flow far better.</p>

                <p><strong>Reach for <code>segmented</code> or <code>pill</code> when the options are really a view toggle, not a content structure</strong><br>
The <code>simple</code> underline variant reads as a structural section divider; <code>segmented</code>/<code>pill</code> read as a mutually-exclusive filter or view switch — pick the one that matches what the tabs are actually doing.</p>

                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The trigger row uses <code>role="tablist"</code> with <code>aria-orientation</code> reflecting <code>orientation</code>. The default <code>aria-label</code> is bilingual ("Tabs" / "علامات التبويب", auto-detected from the document's direction) — override it with <code>label-tablist</code> when the tabs control a specific, nameable region.</li>
<li>Each trigger is a real <code><button></code> with <code>role="tab"</code>, <code>aria-selected</code>, and <code>aria-controls</code> pointing at its panel.</li>
<li>Each panel has <code>role="tabpanel"</code>, <code>aria-labelledby</code> pointing at its trigger, and the native <code>hidden</code> attribute while inactive — genuinely removed from the accessibility tree and from layout, not just visually hidden.</li>
<li>A real roving-tabindex pattern is implemented: only the active trigger has <code>tabindex="0"</code>; every other trigger has <code>tabindex="-1"</code>, so a single <code>Tab</code> press moves focus straight into (and out of) the whole tablist, exactly as the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern specifies.</li>
<li>Disabled tabs set <code>aria-disabled="true"</code> on the trigger rather than the native <code>disabled</code> attribute — deliberately, so the trigger itself remains part of the same roving-tabindex/arrow-key model instead of vanishing from it — and are correctly skipped by arrow-key navigation and unclickable.</li>
<li>Activation follows focus: moving focus to a tab (by click or arrow key) also activates it and reveals its panel immediately — there's no separate "confirm" step.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibility">Developer responsibility</h3>
<p>The following is required for a developer to add additionally or pay attention to regarding this component.</p>
<ul>
<li>Give every <code>aegov-tab</code>/<code>aegov-tab-panel</code> pair a unique, matching <code>tab-id</code>.</li>
<li>Give every trigger a real, meaningful accessible name in its default slot. If a trigger is icon-only, include visually-hidden text alongside the icon rather than relying on the icon alone.</li>
<li>Override <code>label-tablist</code> whenever the tabs control an identifiable region (e.g. <code>"Account sections"</code>) — the bilingual default is a reasonable generic fallback, not a substitute for a specific label.</li>
<li>If a panel holds a heavy asset (a chart, a large image), consider deferring its load until <code>aegovTabChange</code> reports that panel's <code>tab-id</code> as active, rather than loading every panel's content up front.</li>
<li><code>aegov-tab</code> and <code>aegov-tab-panel</code> must be used inside <code>aegov-tabs</code> — <code>aegov-tab-panel</code> throws if it isn't; <code>aegov-tab</code> logs a console error but still renders.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>

<td>Same.</td>

<tr>

<td>Moves to and activates the last tab.</td>
<td>Same.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Tab</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus into the tablist (landing on the active trigger) or out of it entirely — never between individual triggers.</td>
<td>Same.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<p>Arrow-key navigation wraps at both ends and always skips disabled tabs. In a right-to-left document, the horizontal arrows invert — <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> advances and <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> retreats — while vertical navigation, <kbd>Home</kbd>, and <kbd>End</kbd> stay the same in either direction.</p>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-timeline</code> renders a <code><section></code> region landmark wrapping a <code><div role="list"></code> of steps, each step host carrying <code>role="listitem"</code>. Each <code>aegov-timeline-step</code> shows an indicator (a numbered circle or, in <code>compact</code> variant, a small dot), a connector to the step before and after it, and an optional label and description.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/timeline/timeline-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a timeline"></p>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Item</th>
<th>Name</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td><strong>Indicator</strong></td>
<td>The numbered circle (or dot, in compact variant) showing the step's <code>status</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>2</code></td>
<td><strong>Connector</strong></td>
<td>The line between two indicators. Solid when the step before it is <code>completed</code>, dashed otherwise.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td><strong>Label</strong></td>
<td>The step's default-slot text, shown below (horizontal) or beside (vertical) the indicator.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>4</code></td>
<td><strong>Description</strong></td>
<td>Optional supplementary text below the label, from the <code>description</code> prop.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The container renders as a <code><section></code> region landmark whose <code>aria-label</code> defaults to <code>"Timeline"</code> in LTR and <code>"الجدول الزمني"</code> in RTL — no developer translation needed. Pass <code>aria-label</code> on the host to override with a more specific description.</li>
<li>Steps are exposed as a list — the inner container is a <code><div role="list"></code> and each <code>aegov-timeline-step</code> host carries <code>role="listitem"</code> — so screen readers announce the step count and position. (A native <code><ol></code> is not used because it may not contain the custom-element hosts.)</li>
<li>The currently active step's host (its <code>role="listitem"</code> element) carries <code>aria-current="step"</code> — only the step with <code>status="active"</code> has it.</li>
<li>Each step's indicator includes visually hidden text giving its position and status. In the <code>default</code> variant it reads <code>"Step N of M (completed/current)"</code> (Arabic: <code>"الخطوة N من M (مكتمل/الحالية)"</code>), followed by the visible label. In the <code>compact</code> variant, where labels are visually hidden in horizontal mode, it includes the label too: <code>"Step N of M: <label> (completed/current)"</code>. Pending steps get no status suffix.</li>
<li>Decorative connectors and indicator graphics are marked <code>aria-hidden="true"</code>.</li>
<li>If <code>aegov-timeline-step</code> is used outside <code><aegov-timeline></code>, it renders a visible <code>role="alert"</code> configuration-error message instead of a normal step — confirmed live — so a misuse is caught during development rather than silently rendering broken markup.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Provide a meaningful label as default-slot text on every step. The screen-reader description depends on it.</li>
<li>When using a custom <code>icon</code> slot, set <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> on the icon — the step's <code>sr-only</code> label is still rendered regardless.</li>
<li>Keep step ordering meaningful — the visual progression is what gives <code>aria-current="step"</code> value.</li>
<li>Override <code>aria-label</code> on <code><aegov-timeline></code> when more specific context is needed, e.g. <code>aria-label="Application progress"</code> or <code>aria-label="مسار الطلب"</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="notes-2">Notes</h3>
<ul>
<li>The timeline is a presentational component — it does not respond to keyboard or pointer input. If your flow needs clickable step navigation, wrap step content in a button or link, or build a separate interactive stepper.</li>
<li>An unrecognised <code>variant</code>, <code>orientation</code> or step <code>status</code> falls back to its default (<code>default</code>, <code>horizontal</code>, <code>pending</code>) and logs a console warning in development builds only.</li>
<li>Connector colour is computed automatically — confirmed live: the connector before a step renders solid only when the previous step's status is <code>completed</code>, and the connector after a step renders solid only when that step itself is <code>completed</code>.</li>
</ul>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p>A toast is a small card with a coloured top border matching its <code>variant</code>, an optional icon and title, a description, an optional actions row, a dismiss button, and an optional progress bar. Multiple toasts at the same <code>position</code> share a single portal container appended to the end of <code>document.body</code>.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/toast/toast-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a toast"></p>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap="" data-scroll-region="region" tabindex="0" role="region" data-scroll-region-ordinal="1" aria-label="Code example" data-scroll-region-named=""><table>

<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td><strong>Top border</strong></td>
<td>4px coloured strip indicating the <code>variant</code> (<code>error</code>/<code>warning</code>/<code>success</code>/<code>info</code>), or the neutral appearance border for <code>default</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>2</code></td>

<td>Optional, user-provided via the <code>icon</code> slot. No icon ships by default.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td><strong>Title</strong></td>
<td>Optional bold heading via the <code>title</code> slot.</td>

<td>Optional buttons or links via the <code>actions</code> slot — undo, retry, view details.</td>

    <h2 id="basics">Basics</h2>
<p><code>aegov-toast</code> is most often used imperatively through a global helper installed at <code>window.aegovToast</code>. Calling <code>.show(options)</code> creates a toast, mounts it inside a per-position portal container at the end of <code>document.body</code>, and shows it — all in a single call, with no <code><aegov-toast></code> markup or ref required for the common case.</p>

    <h2 id="position">Position</h2>
<p><code>position</code> anchors the toast to a corner or edge of the viewport. Each position has its own portal container, so a single page can run multiple stacks at once — for example a confirmation top-right and a connectivity warning bottom-center.</p>

<td>Aligned to the inline-start of the viewport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

    <h2 id="stack-vs-rack-mode">Stack vs rack mode</h2>
<p>When several toasts land at the same <code>position</code>, <code>mode</code> controls how they lay out. <code>stack</code> (default) shows every toast with a small gap between them. <code>rack</code> collapses them into a single deck — the newest is fully visible, older toasts peek behind it scaled and faded, and a count badge shows the total. Hovering or focusing the deck expands it back into a stack.</p>

    <aegov-button id="mode-rack" variant="primary" field-id="aegov-button-117" class="hydrated">Fire 4 racked toasts</aegov-button>
  </div>

  <script>
    document.getElementById('mode-stack').addEventListener('click', () => {
      ['Application received', 'Documents validated', 'Payment confirmed'].forEach((msg, i) => {
        setTimeout(() => window.aegovToast.show({ message: msg, variant: 'success', mode: 'stack', position: 'top-right', duration: 5000 }), i * 250);

      ['New application received', 'Document uploaded', 'Officer assigned', 'Status updated'].forEach((msg, i) => {
        setTimeout(() => window.aegovToast.show({ message: msg, variant: 'info', mode: 'rack', position: 'bottom-right', duration: 0 }), i * 200);
      });
    });
  </script>

    <h2 id="title-icon-and-actions-slots">Title, icon, and actions slots</h2>
<p>A toast can carry more than description text: <code>title</code> for a bold heading, <code>icon</code> for a custom leading icon (none ships by default), and <code>actions</code> for buttons or links such as an inline undo. These need real slotted markup, added <strong>before</strong> the toast is connected — slot presence and the announced text are both captured when the element loads. A toast declared in plain HTML stays hidden until <code>show()</code> runs, so pre-declared markup works. In a framework app, though, <strong>build the <code><aegov-toast></code> element in your click handler, not as pre-mounted JSX/template markup</strong>: <code>show()</code> moves the element out of the framework's tree and <code>close()</code> removes it from the DOM — construct it on demand instead, exactly as <code>window.aegovToast.show()</code> does internally.</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>
<p>Toast containers use logical CSS properties, so a <code>-right</code> position resolves to the inline-end edge and a <code>-left</code> position to the inline-start edge under RTL. The container and each toast are appended straight to <code>document.body</code>, though — not left inside wherever the trigger button lives — so they only inherit <code>dir</code> from <code><html></code>/<code><body></code>, never from a wrapper placed around the trigger. For a whole Arabic page, set <code>dir="rtl"</code> on <code><html></code> and every toast mirrors automatically. For a single RTL toast on an otherwise-LTR page, set <code>dir="rtl"</code> directly on a declared <code><aegov-toast></code> element, as shown below — the value travels with the element when it moves into its portal container.</p>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Two persistent, reused, visually-hidden live regions exist at the document level: a polite region (<code>role="status"</code>, <code>aria-live="polite"</code>, <code>aria-atomic="true"</code>) for <code>default</code>, <code>info</code>, and <code>success</code> variants, and an assertive region (<code>role="alert"</code>, <code>aria-live="assertive"</code>, <code>aria-atomic="true"</code>) for <code>error</code> and <code>warning</code> variants. <code>show()</code> selects the correct region automatically based on <code>variant</code> and announces the toast's text content as captured when the element loaded — so set the content before adding the toast to the page; text changed afterwards is shown but not announced.</li>
<li>The dismiss button carries a bilingual, variant-aware <code>aria-label</code> — e.g. <code>"Close success notification"</code> in English, <code>"إغلاق إشعار نجاح"</code> in Arabic — with no developer translation needed.</li>
<li>Both mouse hover <strong>and</strong> keyboard focus pause the auto-dismiss timer and progress bar; leaving either resumes it from the exact remaining time (SC 2.2.1) — confirmed live: a toast held past its <code>duration</code> while hovered remained on screen, then closed shortly after the pointer moved away.</li>
<li>In <code>rack</code> mode, the deck expands on hover <strong>or</strong> keyboard focus moving into any toast in the rack, so keyboard users can reach every stacked toast, and collapses only once both leave.</li>
<li>Multiple toasts at the same position are never removed from the DOM while stacked. In <code>rack</code> mode, the newest three stay readable (older ones peek behind, scaled and faded); toasts from the fourth onward are fully hidden and get <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> until the rack expands or newer toasts close. Each toast's live-region announcement still fires when it is shown.</li>
<li>A 300ms exit animation runs before <code>aegovToastClose</code> fires and the element is removed from the DOM.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Keep toast text short and self-contained. Don't use a toast as the only place critical information appears — it can be missed or dismissed.</li>
<li>For confirmations the user must acknowledge, use <code>aegov-modal</code> instead.</li>
<li>Give any button placed in <code>slot="actions"</code> an actionable, descriptive label — "Undo", "View status", "Retry" — not a bare icon.</li>
<li>For a destructive undo affordance, set <code>duration</code> to at least 6000ms so the user has time to react.</li>
<li>Set <code>dir="rtl"</code> directly on a declared <code><aegov-toast></code> element for a single RTL toast — see RTL support above; it will not inherit <code>dir</code> from a wrapper around the trigger, since it and its container move to <code>document.body</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Action</th>

<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus into the toast — its action button(s), then the dismiss button.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the previous focusable element.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Activate the focused button (an action button or the dismiss button).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p>A toggle is a native checkbox with <code>role="switch"</code>, rendered as a rounded track and a circular thumb that slides between OFF and ON. An optional label and hint sit to the side; an optional error message appears below them when the toggle is invalid, with the hint still visible.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/toggle/toggle-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a toggle"></p>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Item</th>
<th>Name</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td><strong>Track</strong></td>
<td>The rounded background. Grey when off; coloured by <code>variant</code> when on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>2</code></td>
<td><strong>Thumb</strong></td>
<td>The circle that slides across the track. Can host an <code>icon-checked</code>/<code>icon-unchecked</code> slot.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td><strong>Label</strong></td>
<td>Optional inline text from the <code>label</code> prop, rendered after the switch. Wraps the whole row in a <code><label></code> when present.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>4</code></td>
<td><strong>Hint</strong></td>
<td>Optional helper text below the label — stays visible while an error shows.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>5</code></td>
<td><strong>Error message</strong></td>
<td>Shown after the hint when <code>is-invalid="true"</code>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>

    <h2 id="basics">Basics</h2>
<p><code>aegov-toggle</code> renders a fully accessible switch on a native <code><input type="checkbox"></code> with <code>role="switch"</code>. Supply <code>label</code> for an inline label and <code>hint</code> for supporting text below it — the label text becomes clickable along with the switch.</p>

    <h2 id="variant">Variant</h2>
<p><code>variant</code> selects the colour family of the ON track, the focus ring, and a thumb icon in the ON state. The OFF track always stays <code>aeblack-100</code> with a 2px <code>aeblack-500</code> inner edge (so the switch keeps 3:1 contrast against the page), and the thumb stays white with a 2px <code>aeblack-500</code> border regardless of variant.</p>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The control is a native <code><input type="checkbox"></code> with <code>role="switch"</code> and an explicit <code>aria-checked</code> state, so assistive technology announces "switch, on"/"switch, off" rather than "checkbox, checked".</li>
<li>When <code>hint</code> (or the <code>hint</code> slot) is provided, the input is linked to it via <code>aria-describedby</code> so screen readers read the helper text after the label. The same applies to the error message when shown — the hint stays visible alongside the error, and the description reads the error, then the hint.</li>
<li><code>is-required</code> sets both the native <code>required</code> attribute and <code>aria-required="true"</code>.</li>
<li>The error region only takes <code>role="alert"</code> after the user has blurred the field at least once, so a validation message present at initial load isn't announced as an interruption — confirmed live: a toggle rendered with <code>is-invalid</code> from the start shows the error text immediately but without <code>role="alert"</code>, which appears only after the first blur.</li>
<li>When <code>label</code> is supplied, the switch and its text are wrapped in a <code><label></code>, so clicking the label text — not just the switch itself — toggles the control. The clickable area is at least 24px tall at every size.</li>
<li><code>aria-checked</code>, the inner input's <code>checked</code> state, and the <code>isChecked</code> JS property always stay correct and in sync on every interaction — confirmed live across repeated toggling.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Always provide <code>label</code>, or when the toggle must render as a bare switch, link an external label via <code>aria-labelledby</code>. A switch without an accessible name is opaque to screen reader users.</li>
<li>Use a toggle only for settings that take effect immediately. For "save later" choices, use a checkbox.</li>
<li>Keep <code>icon-checked</code>/<code>icon-unchecked</code> decorative — the state is already announced via <code>aria-checked</code>. Don't encode the toggle's only meaning in the icon.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>

<td>Toggle the switch on or off.</td>

</tr>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-checkbox</code> renders a native <code><input type="checkbox"></code>, optionally wrapped in a <code><label></code> when <code>label</code> is set, with the hint and error message as sibling regions. <code>aegov-checkbox-group</code> renders a native <code><fieldset></code>/<code><legend></code> around a set of checkboxes, plus its own shared hint and error regions.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/checkbox/checkbox-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a checkbox"></p>

    <h2 id="label-and-hint">Label and hint</h2>
<p>Set <code>label</code> to render a clickable <code><label></code> around the control. Add <code>hint</code> for supporting helper text underneath — it stays visible while a validation error shows, because that is when the user needs it most. Omit <code>label</code> entirely for a bare checkbox (for example, inside a table row with its own column heading) and supply your own <code>aria-label</code> instead.</p>

    <h2 id="select-all">Select all</h2>
<p>Mark one checkbox in a group <code>is-check-all</code> to turn it into a select-all controller. It automatically checks or unchecks every other (enabled) checkbox in the group, and reflects back to indeterminate whenever only some — but not all — of them are checked. This cascades in both directions: toggling the controller toggles the children, and toggling any child updates the controller.</p>

    <h2 id="group-disabled">Group disabled</h2>
<p>Set <code>is-disabled</code> on <code>aegov-checkbox-group</code> to disable every checkbox inside it at once — the group both wraps its own <code><fieldset disabled></code> and cascades <code>is-disabled</code> to each child's own prop, so no need to set it individually. Toggling the group's <code>is-disabled</code> back off restores each child's own <code>is-disabled</code> setting, so a child that was disabled on its own stays disabled.</p>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>aegov-checkbox</code> renders a real native <code><input type="checkbox"></code>, so keyboard toggling (<kbd>Space</kbd>), focus handling, and assistive-technology announcements all come for free.</li>
<li>Setting <code>label</code> wraps the input in a real <code><label></code>, so clicking or tapping the text also toggles the control — no manual <code>for</code>/<code>id</code> wiring needed.</li>
<li><code>is-indeterminate</code> sets the native <code>indeterminate</code> DOM property (not just a visual style) and reflects <code>aria-checked="mixed"</code>, so screen readers announce the true tri-state correctly.</li>
<li><code>aegov-checkbox-group</code> renders a native <code><fieldset></code>/<code><legend></code> pair when <code>label</code> is set, giving the whole group a single accessible name without extra ARIA wiring.</li>
<li>Hint and error text are wired to the input (or fieldset) via <code>aria-describedby</code> automatically whenever <code>hint</code>/<code>error-message</code> (or their slots) are present — you never need to manage the id linkage yourself. The hint stays visible while an error shows, so the description reads the error, then the hint.</li>
<li>The error region only takes <code>role="alert"</code> after the user has actually interacted with the field once (blurred it, or interacted with the group), so a validation message present at initial page load is not announced as an interruption.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibility">Developer responsibility</h3>
<p>The following is required for a developer to add additionally or pay attention to regarding this component.</p>
<ul>
<li>If you omit <code>label</code> (for example, a checkbox inside a data-table row with a visible column heading), supply <code>aria-label</code> or <code>aria-labelledby</code> yourself — the component does not fall back to any other accessible name.</li>
<li>When using <code>is-check-all</code>, give it its own descriptive <code>label</code> (e.g. "Select all services") — its relationship to the other items is conveyed by DOM position and indeterminate state, not announced automatically.</li>
<li><code>is-indeterminate</code> is a visual/state hint only, never a substitute for <code>is-required</code> or real validation — a required checkbox group still needs at least one real checked value to pass validation.</li>
<li><code>is-required</code> on <code>aegov-checkbox-group</code> does not block a native form submit, and it shows no error by itself: the group isn't part of the browser's form validation. On submit, call <code>await group.validate('submit')</code>; if the result isn't <code>valid</code>, prevent the submit, set <code>error-message</code> (for example from <code>result.message</code>) and <code>is-invalid</code> on the group, and move focus to the first checkbox in the group. Clear them when the user makes a choice. See the <a href="/docs/concepts/validation#whole-form-validation-on-submit">whole-form validation pattern</a>.</li>
<li>Check colour contrast for any custom <code>extra-class</code> background or text colour against your chosen <code>variant</code> — the component does not validate this for you.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="additional-notes">Additional notes</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>size</code> on both components accepts a responsive breakpoint string, the same convention used by Badge, Banner, and Callout (e.g. <code>size="sm md:base"</code>).</li>
<li><code>appearance</code> on <code>aegov-checkbox</code> is written by its parent group and shouldn't be set directly — set <code>appearance</code> on the <code>aegov-checkbox-group</code> instead. A standalone checkbox with no parent group always renders <code>default</code>.</li>
<li><code>name</code>/form submission are handled via <code>ElementInternals</code> on the host element, not the inner shadow-DOM <code><input></code> — reading <code>checkbox.name</code> or checking form data works exactly like a native input, but querying the shadow DOM's own <code><input></code> for <code>name</code> will come back empty. This is expected, not a bug.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>

                <h1 class="text-h3 lg:text-h2 xl:text-h1 mb-4 text-primary-700">Datepicker</h1>
                <p class="text-base lg:text-lg leading-normal text-aeblack-600">A Datepicker lets a user pick a single date, or a start and end date for a range, from a calendar dialog instead of typing free text. "aegov-datepicker" renders a read-only trigger input and opens its calendar in a portal attached to the end of the page, so the calendar is never clipped by a card, modal, or any other "overflow: hidden" ancestor. Single-date and date-range selection share one component, with full keyboard navigation, presets, blackout dates, range limits, and an optional Apply / Cancel confirmation flow.</p>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-datepicker</code> renders a styled trigger — one input in single mode, two in range mode — plus a calendar dialog that opens in a portal at the end of <code>document.body</code>, not inline in the surrounding layout.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/datepicker/datepicker-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a datepicker"></p>

    <h2 id="variant">Variant</h2>
<p><code>variant</code> selects the colour family for the trigger's idle border, the selected day fill, the today indicator, and the hover background. The focus ring uses the variant's own support colour (<code>primary-support-500</code> / <code>secondary-support-500</code> / <code>seablue-500</code> for both neutral variants, one step lighter in dark mode); the error border stays <code>aered-600</code> regardless of variant.</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>
<p>When the host (or an ancestor) is <code>dir="rtl"</code>, the portaled calendar mirrors its layout: the second calendar in range mode swaps sides, the presets sidebar moves to the opposite edge, and the prev/next chevron icons swap so they still point in the reading direction. Without <code>locale</code>, month and weekday names and the datepicker's own text follow the page language — the nearest <code>lang</code>, or <code>dir="rtl"</code> when no <code>lang</code> is set — so an Arabic page gets Arabic text throughout; <code>locale="ar"</code> forces it. Left/Right arrow keys follow the visual direction, and the calendar portal carries the same <code>dir</code> and <code>lang</code>. Add <code>start-day="6"</code> to match the UAE week convention.</p>

                <section class="article-section">
                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The trigger has <code>role="combobox"</code>, <code>aria-haspopup="dialog"</code>, <code>aria-expanded</code>, and <code>aria-controls</code> (pointing at the dialog when open), so screen readers announce the calendar relationship.</li>
<li>The portal calendar renders as <code>role="dialog"</code> with <code>aria-modal="true"</code>, labelled via <code>aria-labelledby</code> pointing at a visually-hidden element showing the current month and year — it updates as the user navigates months.</li>
<li>A polite <code>aria-live</code> region inside the portal announces month changes and range-limit messages (the focused day itself is read from its button, so it is not repeated). A second live region on the host (outside the portal) announces the final confirmed selection after the calendar closes, so the announcement survives the portal being torn down.</li>
<li>The calendar grid has <code>role="grid"</code>; each day is a <code>role="gridcell"</code> containing a button with a full-date <code>aria-label</code> (e.g. "Tuesday, September 8, 2026"). Unavailable dates append ", unavailable" to their label.</li>
<li>Day buttons expose <code>aria-selected</code> on their gridcell, <code>aria-current="date"</code> for today, and <code>aria-disabled</code> for blackout / out-of-range dates. Unavailable days stay focusable (no native <code>disabled</code>), so arrow-key navigation never strands focus, but they cannot be chosen.</li>
<li>Navigation chevron icons are <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> — the prev/next buttons carry their own bilingual <code>aria-label</code> ("Previous month, May 2026" style), not the icon.</li>
<li>Preset buttons expose <code>aria-pressed</code> to reflect whether they match the current selection. The presets sidebar has <code>role="group"</code> with its own <code>aria-label</code>.</li>
<li>Focus moves into the calendar on open (the selected day, the range start, or today) and returns on close to the element that was focused before opening (else the field), using roving <code>tabindex</code> within the grid so only one day is ever in the tab order at a time.</li>
<li>The trigger's inner input is <code>readOnly</code> — users cannot type free-form text and produce an invalid date; every selection happens through the dialog.</li>
<li>The calendar closes automatically if its trigger scrolls out of the viewport, and re-positions on every scroll and resize.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Always give the datepicker a visible label: put it in <code>aegov-form-field</code> with an <code>aegov-label</code>. The label becomes the field's accessible name (in range mode it is combined with <code>label-range-start</code> / <code>label-range-end</code>, e.g. "Leave dates, Leave start"). A <code>placeholder</code> or the range labels alone are not enough: they are hidden once a date is chosen, so the field's purpose is no longer visible (WCAG 3.3.2). Use <code>aria-label</code> on the host only when a visible label is truly not possible, such as a custom icon trigger.</li>
<li><code>blackout</code> only accepts an explicit, literal list of ISO dates — there is no recurring-exclusion syntax (no "every weekend", no "every Friday"). A recurring closure schedule must be enumerated into individual dates by your own code before being passed in.</li>
<li>In range mode, a second click that would violate <code>min-range</code> / <code>max-range</code> is refused: the start date stays, and a message such as "Range must be at least 3 days" shows under the months and is announced. State the allowed range in <code>hint</code> as well, so users know it before they open the calendar.</li>
<li>If you supply a custom trigger via the <code>trigger</code> slot, make sure it is itself a focusable, named element — the component does not add tab-stop behaviour to arbitrary slotted content. <code>is-disabled</code> stops clicks but not <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on a focusable custom trigger, so disable the trigger element as well.</li>
<li>In Arabic contexts, set <code>dir="rtl"</code> (and <code>lang="ar"</code>) on the host or an ancestor for the right-to-left layout — the built-in text, month and day names then follow the page language without <code>locale</code>; set <code>locale="ar"</code> only to force Arabic regardless of the page (<code>locale</code> does not change direction). Set <code>start-day="6"</code> to match the UAE week convention.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Opens the calendar from the trigger; picks the focused day inside the calendar.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Arrow Left</code> / <code>Right</code></td>
<td>Moves the focused day by one column (mirrors direction in RTL).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Arrow Up</code> / <code>Down</code></td>
<td>Moves the focused day by one week.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Page Up</code> / <code>Down</code></td>
<td>Moves the focused day by one month.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Shift + Page Up</code> / <code>Down</code></td>
<td>Moves the focused day by one year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Home</code> / <code>End</code></td>
<td>Moves to the first / last day of the current week.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Escape</code></td>
<td>Closes the calendar without committing (discards pending state in confirmation mode).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Cycles only through the calendar's own focusable elements while open (a focus trap).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-fileupload</code> wraps a real native <code><input type="file"></code>. Depending on <code>appearance</code>, the visible control is a styled input row with a trailing browse button, a stand-alone trigger button with a file list beneath it, or a bordered drag-and-drop dropzone.</p>

    <h2 id="appearances">Appearances</h2>
<p><code>appearance</code> selects the layout. All three share the same validation, events, and form behaviour — only the visual presentation differs. <code>default</code> looks like a styled text input with a trailing Browse button, and replaces the whole selection on each pick — best for a single required document inside a dense form. <code>button</code> renders a stand-alone trigger button with picked files listed below it, accumulating across picks. <code>dropzone</code> renders a large drag-and-drop target with a fallback browse button, also accumulating — best for a high-volume upload step.</p>

    <h2 id="file-type-and-size-validation">File type and size validation</h2>
<p>Set <code>accept</code> to a comma-separated list of extensions, MIME types, or wildcards. The component enforces it both as a filter hint to the OS picker and again after selection — the OS picker's own filter can usually be bypassed by the user, so the second check matters. Set <code>max-file-size</code> in bytes to reject oversized files.     <h2 id="multiple-files-and-maximum-count">Multiple files and maximum count</h2>
<p>Set <code>is-multiple="true"</code> to let the picker return more than one file at a time (and let the dropzone accept several dropped files). Pair it with <code>max-files</code> to cap the total — once the cap is reached, further picks beyond it are not added, and a notice under the field names the files that were left out. Picking a file with the same name as one already in the list replaces that entry rather than adding a duplicate.</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>
<p>The component is direction-agnostic — every layout works the same way under <code>dir="rtl"</code>, reading its computed direction from the nearest ancestor the same way any real element does (there is no portal involved, so this always works). In the default appearance, the browse button keeps its position at the trailing edge of the row relative to the reading direction, which is the physical left in RTL. Built-in strings — button text, "No file chosen", the drag-and-drop prompt, the "Allowed: …" summary, file sizes, rejection and max-files messages, "Required" and "Remove {filename}" — switch to Arabic when the nearest <code>dir</code> (or <code><html dir></code>) is <code>rtl</code>; <code>lang</code> alone does not switch them. Supply Arabic <code>label</code>, <code>hint</code>, <code>label-help</code> and <code>label-button</code> text yourself for a fully localized field.</p>

                <p><strong>Do not rely on the OS picker's <code>accept</code> filter alone</strong><br>
The browser's file dialog filter is a convenience, not a guarantee — most OS pickers let a user override it and choose "All files". <code>aegov-fileupload</code> re-validates every picked file against <code>accept</code> after selection; never assume the filter alone was enough if you're validating independently downstream.</p>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>The control is anchored on a real <code><input type="file"></code>, so it is keyboard-focusable, screen-reader-friendly, and submits with native forms via <code>ElementInternals</code>.</li>
<li>Default appearance: the visible <code>label</code> is a real <code><label for></code> on the native input. Button and dropzone appearances: the label names the <code>role="group"</code> around the trigger, and the trigger button's name is its visible text followed by the label (for example "Browse Files, Supporting documents"), so speech-input users can say what they see. A label from <code>aegov-form-field</code>, or <code>aria-label</code> / <code>aria-labelledby</code> on the host, is used the same way.</li>
<li>Default appearance: the native input carries <code>aria-invalid</code> and an <code>aria-describedby</code> linking "Required" (when <code>is-required</code> is set — a file input can't take <code>aria-required</code>), the allowed-types summary, the error and the hint, directly on the visible, focusable control. Its accessible name includes the visible "Browse" text after the label, so speech-input users can say "click Browse".</li>
<li>Button and dropzone appearances: the native input is visually hidden (<code>aria-hidden</code>, <code>tabindex="-1"</code>) behind a real <code>aegov-button</code>, inside the named group. The trigger button itself carries <code>aria-invalid</code> and an <code>aria-description</code> that reads the current selection, "Required", the allowed types, the error and the hint, so assistive tech announces the field's state on the control that has focus.</li>
<li>The error region gets <code>role="alert"</code> once the user has interacted with the field at least once, so a validation message already present at initial load doesn't interrupt assistive tech on page arrival.</li>
<li>Each file's remove button has a bilingual <code>aria-label</code> ("Remove {filename}"); its icon is <code>aria-hidden="true"</code>.</li>
<li>Added and removed files are announced through a polite status message ("passport.pdf added (1 file)", "passport.pdf removed"), in Arabic when the field is inside <code>dir="rtl"</code>, otherwise in English.</li>
<li>In the button and dropzone appearances, picking a file with the same name as one already in the list replaces that entry instead of adding it twice.</li>
<li>With <code>max-files</code>, files over the limit are not added: a visible notice under the list names them ("report.pdf not added: maximum 3 files.") and is announced. It is a notice, not an error, so the field is not marked invalid.</li>
<li>The native input's value is reset after every pick, so selecting the exact same file again still fires <code>aegovFileuploadChange</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Always set a real <code>label</code> (or pair with an external <code>aegov-label</code>) — the control has no other fallback accessible name.</li>
<li>For <code>appearance="dropzone"</code>, drag-and-drop is a pointer-only enhancement; the fallback browse button is the accessible way in for keyboard and touch users. Never remove it.</li>
<li>Use <code>error-message</code> or the <code>error</code> slot to surface validation messages — both are announced with the control automatically, alongside the hint, which stays visible.</li>
<li>The component only selects files; it does not upload them. When your code uploads the files, show the progress and the result for each one (for example "Uploading 2 of 3", "passport.pdf uploaded", "passport.pdf failed, the file is too large") and announce those changes in a polite live region (<code>role="status"</code>) so screen-reader users hear them without moving focus (WCAG 4.1.3). Report a failed upload with <code>error-message</code> and <code>is-invalid</code>, and give the user a way to retry or remove the file.</li>
<li><code>appearance="default"</code> replaces the entire selection on each pick; <code>button</code> and <code>dropzone</code> accumulate. Call <code>clear()</code> to reset programmatically.</li>
<li>The OS file picker's own type filter (built from <code>accept</code>) can usually be bypassed by the user (most pickers offer an "All files" option) — the component re-validates every picked file after selection regardless, so don't skip <code>accept</code> even if you also validate server-side.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code> / <code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Moves focus into the control, between picked files' remove buttons, and to the next/previous focusable element.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Opens the OS file picker when the trigger (native input, in default appearance, or the browse/dropzone button) is focused.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Removes the focused file when a remove button is focused.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-input</code> renders a real native <code><input></code> inside a small wrapper that adds icon slots and, for password/copyable fields, an inset action button.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/input/input-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of an input"></p>

<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td><strong>Icon slot</strong></td>
<td>Optional leading icon (<code>icon-start</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>2</code></td>
<td><strong>Native input</strong></td>
<td>The real <code><input></code> element — receives all typing, autofill, and focus</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td><strong>Action button</strong></td>
<td>Password reveal or copy-to-clipboard button, inset at the trailing edge</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>4</code></td>
<td><strong>Hint / error region</strong></td>
<td>Validation text, then helper text, rendered below the field — the hint stays visible while an error shows</td>

    <h2 id="input-types">Input types</h2>
<p><code>type</code> maps directly to the native HTML input type. Use <code>text</code> for general fields, <code>email</code> for addresses (triggers email keyboards on mobile), <code>tel</code> for phone numbers, <code>number</code> for fees and amounts, and <code>search</code>/<code>url</code> for the obvious cases.</p>

    <h2 id="input-group-with-add-ons">Input group with add-ons</h2>
<p><code>aegov-input-group</code> wraps an <code>aegov-input</code> (and optionally an <code>aegov-button</code>) to add a static prefix and/or suffix, or a trailing action button. It propagates its <code>size</code> to every child so everything lines up, and its <code>variant</code> cascades to a child that hasn't set its own. The prefix and suffix text is added to the input's description, so a screen reader announces it with the field. Inside a group, the child input's hint or error is shown below the whole group, and while the input is invalid the group shows the error in place of the hint.</p>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>aegov-input</code> renders a real native <code><input></code>, preserving native semantics, keyboard handling, autofill, and assistive-technology behaviour.</li>
<li>The label reaches the native <code><input></code> inside the shadow DOM. ID references can't cross that boundary on their own, so the component resolves each naming source to text and gives it to the inner input: <code>aegov-label</code> inside <code>aegov-form-field</code>, an <code>aegov-label for="…"</code> pointing at the host's <code>id</code> or <code>field-id</code>, a native <code><label for="…"></code> pointing at the host's <code>id</code>, and <code>aria-label</code> / <code>aria-labelledby</code> set on the host.</li>
<li>An <code>aria-describedby</code> you set on the host is handled the same way: the referenced text becomes part of the input's description, read before the component's own error and hint.</li>
<li><code>is-required</code> sets the native <code>required</code> attribute, exposing the requirement to assistive tech automatically.</li>
<li>The reveal and copy buttons each carry a descriptive, bilingual <code>aria-label</code> ("Show password"/"Hide password", "Copy to clipboard") and sit in the natural tab order. The copy button keeps its name after a copy; a visually hidden <code>role="status"</code> region announces "Copied" instead.</li>
<li>Decorative SVG icons inside the reveal/copy buttons are <code>aria-hidden="true"</code>.</li>
<li><code>hint</code>/<code>error-message</code> (or the <code>hint</code>/<code>error</code> slots), when set directly on <code>aegov-input</code>, are wired to the native input's <code>aria-describedby</code> automatically (the hint stays visible and described while an error shows), and the error region only takes <code>role="alert"</code> after the user has blurred the field once, the form has reported it invalid (on submit or <code>checkValidity()</code>), or <code>validate('submit')</code> has run — so a validation message present at initial load isn't announced as an interruption.</li>
<li><code>aegov-input-group</code> renders <code>role="group"</code> and forwards consumer <code>aria-*</code> attributes to it, except <code>aria-label</code>; use <code>group-label</code> for the accessible name, or add your own <code>aria-labelledby</code> to reference an external heading.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Always provide a visible label — <code>aegov-label</code> inside <code>aegov-form-field</code> is the preferred pattern. For an unlabelled input (e.g. an icon-only search field), set <code>aria-label</code> on the host yourself.</li>
<li>Place hint/error content as a direct child of <code>aegov-input</code> itself (or use the plain-text <code>hint</code>/<code>error-message</code> props) — content placed elsewhere, such as a plain paragraph beside <code>aegov-input</code> inside <code>aegov-form-field</code>, is not linked to the field. (An element in <code>aegov-form-field</code>'s own <code>hint</code> slot is the exception: the wrapper links it to the input for you.)</li>
<li>Choose the right <code>type</code> for the data being collected — it drives on-screen keyboards, autofill, and built-in validation.</li>
<li>Set <code>autocomplete</code> on fields that collect the user's own details — for example <code>autocomplete="name"</code>, <code>"email"</code>, <code>"tel"</code>, <code>"street-address"</code>, <code>"postal-code"</code> — so the browser can fill them in and users don't have to retype them (WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose). The attribute is passed through to the native input.</li>
<li>For password reveal, remember the toggle only changes what's visible locally — it doesn't warn anyone else who might be looking at the screen.</li>
<li>For copyable fields, make sure the value is safe to sit in the user's clipboard history.</li>
<li>Handle form submission yourself. When the browser blocks a submit (for example a required field is empty), it only shows its own temporary bubble, in the browser's language: the field gets no error text on the page and no <code>aria-invalid</code>. Use the <a href="/docs/concepts/validation#whole-form-validation-on-submit">whole-form validation pattern</a>: on submit, call <code>validate('submit')</code> on each field and set <code>is-invalid</code> and <code>error-message</code> from the result, so every error is shown, announced and stays on screen.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus into the input, then to the reveal/copy button (if shown), then to the next field.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the previous focusable element.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code></td>
<td>Commit the value (fires <code>aegovInputChange</code>) and submits the surrounding form.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Standard text editing</td>
<td>All native shortcuts apply — selection, cursor movement, cut/copy/paste.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-otp</code> renders a <code>role="group"</code> wrapper around a row of real <code><input type="text"></code> cells — one per character. Typing a valid character auto-advances focus to the next cell; the assembled value across all cells is exposed as a single logical field, both through events and through native <code><form></code> submission via <code>ElementInternals</code> (no hidden input needed).</p>

    <h2 id="uae-pass-mfa-verification-example">UAE Pass MFA verification example</h2>
<p>A typical UAE Government scenario: confirming a UAE Pass two-factor authentication code sent by SMS. This composes <code>aegov-otp</code> with a real <code>aegov-label</code> (linked via <code>field-id</code>), wires <code>aegovOtpComplete</code> to kick off verification and <code>aegovValidate</code> to react to a pattern failure, and calls <code>.clear()</code> from a "resend code" button.</p>

</div>

        <div style="width:100%;">
  <aegov-label field-id="mfa-demo" class="hydrated"><!----><label id="mfa-demo" class="aegov-label label-variant-primary">Enter the 6-digit code sent to your UAE Pass mobile number</label></aegov-label>
  <aegov-otp id="mfa-otp-demo" field-id="mfa-demo" length="6" pattern="^[0-9]{6}$" name="mfa_code" class="hydrated"></aegov-otp>
  <p id="mfa-status-demo" class="mt-3 text-sm text-aeblack-600">Waiting for code…</p>
  <aegov-button id="mfa-resend-demo" variant="secondary" appearance="outline" size="sm" class="mt-3 hydrated" field-id="aegov-button-208">Resend code</aegov-button>
  <script>
    (function () {
      const otp = document.getElementById('mfa-otp-demo');
      const status = document.getElementById('mfa-status-demo');
      otp.addEventListener('aegovOtpComplete', (e) => {
        status.textContent = 'Verifying ' + e.detail.value + '…';
        status.className = 'mt-3 text-sm text-techblue-600';
      });
      otp.addEventListener('aegovValidate', (e) => {
        if (e.detail.validity.patternMismatch) {
          status.textContent = 'That code is not valid. Please try again.';
          status.className = 'mt-3 text-sm text-aered-600';
        }
      });
      document.getElementById('mfa-resend-demo').addEventListener('click', () => {
        otp.clear();
        status.textContent = 'Waiting for code…';
        status.className = 'mt-3 text-sm text-aeblack-600';
      });
    })();
  </script>
</div>

<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Each cell is a real <code><input type="text"></code> with <code>inputmode="numeric"</code> (or <code>text</code> when <code>is-alphanumeric</code>), so mobile devices show the matching keyboard.</li>
<li>The first cell carries <code>autocomplete="one-time-code"</code>, enabling iOS/Android SMS autofill.</li>
<li>All cells sit inside a <code>role="group"</code> element so screen readers treat them as one field. Each cell has its own <code>aria-label</code> — "Character N of L" (Arabic: "حرف N من L") — so a user knows their position. Each cell is its own tab stop.</li>
<li>Every cell carries <code>aria-invalid</code>/<code>aria-required</code>/<code>aria-describedby</code> (pointing at the error and hint regions), so a user correcting any cell hears the error and hint, not just on the first one. Error styling also applies to every cell.</li>
<li>The error region only gets <code>role="alert"</code> once focus has left the whole group at least once (or the form has reported it invalid, or <code>validate('submit')</code> has run) — this avoids interrupting the user with an announcement while they're still mid-way through typing between cells. The error text itself is still visible immediately; only the live-region announcement is deferred.</li>
<li>Focus auto-advances to the next cell after a valid character, and steps back to (and clears) the previous cell on <code>Backspace</code> when the current cell is already empty.</li>
<li>Paste fills from the first cell, ignores whitespace, and rejects characters that fail the numeric/alphanumeric rule. A whole code entered into a later cell (autofill, dictation, a password manager) also fills from the first cell.</li>
<li>The cells always run left to right, even on RTL pages — codes read left to right in every language. Cell labels and messages stay in the page language, and the built-in validation messages ("Enter 6 characters", "Invalid format") are translated on Arabic pages.</li>
<li>Form participation is handled via <code>ElementInternals</code> — the assembled value submits as a single field with no visible hidden input.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Pair the OTP with a real <code>aegov-label</code> linked via <code>field-id</code> — each cell's own <code>aria-label</code> only describes position, not purpose.</li>
<li>Use <code>pattern</code> only as a fast client-side failure signal; always verify the code server-side.</li>
<li>Provide a way to resend the code and a way to reset the field — call <code>.clear()</code> on the element.</li>
<li>Show the error yourself. The OTP doesn't display a message on its own: <code>validate()</code> and the <code>aegovValidate</code> event only report the result (<code>detail.validity</code>, <code>detail.validationMessage</code>). When the code is incomplete or wrong (on submit, or when the server rejects it), set <code>error-message</code> and <code>is-invalid</code> so the message is shown under the cells and announced, and clear them when the user edits the code. Without that, a wrong code shows nothing and screen-reader users hear nothing (WCAG 3.3.1).</li>
<li>Check the field on a 320 px wide screen. The cells shrink to fit instead of scrolling sideways, down to a 24 px minimum, so for long codes (8 or more characters) choose <code>size="base"</code> or smaller to keep every digit easy to read and tap (WCAG 1.4.10).</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Action</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>0</code>–<code>9</code>, <code>A</code>–<code>Z</code> (alphanumeric mode)</td>
<td>Enter a character. Auto-advances focus to the next cell.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Backspace</code></td>
<td>Clear the current cell, or — when it's already empty — clear and move focus to the previous cell.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowLeft</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the previous cell (also in RTL — the cells never mirror).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowRight</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next cell (also in RTL).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Home</code> / <code>End</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the first/last cell.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Ctrl</code>/<code>Cmd</code> + <code>V</code></td>
<td>Paste the code; characters distribute across cells from the first one.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code> / <code>Shift+Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next/previous cell — each cell is its own tab stop — and out of the OTP after the last/before the first cell.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<h3 id="notes-2">Notes</h3>
<ul>
<li>An unrecognised <code>appearance</code>, <code>variant</code>, or <code>size</code> value falls back to its default.</li>
<li><code>pattern</code> is only checked once every cell is filled — a partially-filled value never triggers a pattern failure, only <code>tooShort</code>.</li>
</ul>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-popover</code> wraps a trigger element (its default slot) and, while open, renders its <code>popover-content</code> slot into a portal at <code>document.body</code> — positioned next to the trigger with a small directional arrow, so it can escape any clipping or stacking context on the page.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/popover/popover-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a popover"></p>

    <h2 id="basic-popover">Basic popover</h2>
<p>Place a trigger in the default slot and the panel content in the <code>popover-content</code> slot. By default the popover opens on click, traps focus while open, and closes on <code>Escape</code>, an outside click, or when the trigger scrolls out of view.</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>
<p>The popover's own positioning is direction-aware: it reads direction from the host's own ancestor chain (which is never moved — only the panel content is portalled), so <code>position</code>'s absolute viewport sides (<code>top</code>/<code>right</code>/<code>bottom</code>/<code>left</code>) stay fixed, while <code>align="start"</code>/<code>"end"</code> correctly follow the reading direction for <code>top</code>/<code>bottom</code>. The portal also copies the host's computed direction as <code>dir</code> each time it opens, so content inside a local <code>dir="rtl"</code> wrapper stays right-to-left in the panel even though it is moved to <code>document.body</code>.</p>
