                <section class="article-section">
                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>aria-haspopup="dialog"</code> and <code>aria-expanded</code> are set on the first real focusable element inside the trigger slot (not just the wrapper), including reaching inside a shadow-DOM trigger like <code>aegov-button</code>.</li>
<li>The portalled panel renders with <code>role="dialog"</code> and is labelled by the trigger via <code>aria-labelledby</code>.</li>
<li>For <code>trigger="click"</code>, opening moves focus to the first focusable element inside the panel; with no focusable content, the panel container itself receives focus so assistive technology still announces it.</li>
<li><code>Tab</code>/<code>Shift+Tab</code> and <code>ArrowUp</code>/<code>ArrowDown</code> all cycle focus through the focusable elements inside the panel while it's open. Only light-DOM focusable elements (native links, buttons, inputs) are found — shadow-DOM components such as <code>aegov-button</code> inside the panel are not focused on open or reached with <code>Tab</code>.</li>
<li><code>Escape</code> closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger.</li>
<li>For <code>trigger="hover"</code>, the popover also opens on keyboard focus and closes on blur (so hover is never the only way in) — focus deliberately stays on the trigger itself rather than moving into the panel, since this pattern is a hovercard, not a dialog.</li>
<li>Clicking outside the trigger and panel closes the popover; scrolling the trigger out of the viewport closes it too.</li>
<li>Only one popover can be open at a time — opening a new one closes whichever was already open.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Give an icon-only trigger a real <code>aria-label</code> — the panel is labelled through the trigger, so this one attribute covers both.</li>
<li>Keep popover content compact and self-contained; move to <code>aegov-modal</code>/<code>aegov-drawer</code> once it grows into a real form or multi-step flow.</li>
<li>Mark up list-style content with <code><ul></code>/<code><li></code> and real links so keyboard users can move through it naturally.</li>
<li>If the panel has a heading, pick the level that follows the surrounding section (an <code><h3></code> under an <code><h2></code>), not a smaller one for its size; style the size with classes.</li>
<li>Use native <code><a href></code>, <code><button></code> and <code><input></code> elements inside the panel so its focus handling can reach them, and avoid controls that need arrow keys (a select or textarea) — <code>ArrowUp</code>/<code>ArrowDown</code> move focus between panel controls while it is open.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Action</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Open the popover when the (click) trigger is focused.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code> (into trigger)</td>
<td>Opens the popover when <code>trigger="hover"</code> (keyboard-focus equivalent of hover). While a hover popover is open, <code>Tab</code> stays on the trigger — press <code>Escape</code> first to move on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Escape</code></td>
<td>Close the popover and return focus to the trigger.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code> / <code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Cycle through focusable elements inside the open panel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowDown</code> / <code>ArrowUp</code></td>
<td>Move to the next/previous focusable element inside the open panel.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<h3 id="notes-2">Notes</h3>
<ul>
<li>An unrecognised <code>trigger</code>, <code>position</code>, or <code>align</code> value falls back to its documented default.</li>
<li>Popover content is moved — not cloned — into the portal while open, and returned to its original slot location when closed. Avoid styling it with anything that depends on its original parent's layout context.</li>
</ul>

</div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-radio</code> renders a native <code><input type="radio"></code>, optionally wrapped in a <code><label></code> when <code>label</code> is set, with the hint and error message as sibling regions. <code>aegov-radio-group</code> renders a native <code><fieldset></code>/<code><legend></code> (with <code>role="radiogroup"</code>) around a set of radios, plus its own shared hint and error regions.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/radio/radio-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a radio"></p>

                <section class="article-section">
                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>aegov-radio</code> renders a real native <code><input type="radio"></code>, so basic toggling and assistive-technology announcement as a radio button come for free.</li>
<li>Setting <code>label</code> wraps the input in a real <code><label></code>, so clicking or tapping the text also selects the control — no manual <code>for</code>/<code>id</code> wiring needed.</li>
<li><code>aegov-radio-group</code> renders a native <code><fieldset></code>/<code><legend></code> pair (with <code>role="radiogroup"</code>) when <code>label</code> is set, giving the whole group a single accessible name without extra ARIA wiring.</li>
<li>Hint and error text are wired to the input (or fieldset) via <code>aria-describedby</code> automatically whenever <code>hint</code>/<code>error-message</code> (or their slots) are present. The hint stays visible while an error shows, so the description reads the error, then the hint.</li>
<li><code>aegov-radio-group</code> implements the WAI-ARIA radio group keyboard pattern: the group is a single tab stop and the arrow keys move both focus and selection between options.</li>
<li>The error region only takes <code>role="alert"</code> after the user has actually interacted with the field once (blurred it, or interacted with the group), so a validation message present at initial page load is not announced as an interruption.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibility">Developer responsibility</h3>
<p>The following is required for a developer to add additionally or pay attention to regarding this component.</p>
<ul>
<li>If you omit <code>label</code>, supply <code>aria-label</code> or <code>aria-labelledby</code> yourself — the component does not fall back to any other accessible name.</li>
<li>Always wrap related radios in <code>aegov-radio-group</code> and set the group <code>label</code> — this gives assistive technology the question being asked, not just each option's own text.</li>
<li><code>is-required</code> on <code>aegov-radio-group</code> does not block a native form submit, and it shows no error by itself: the group isn't part of the browser's form validation. On submit, call <code>await group.validate('submit')</code>; if the result isn't <code>valid</code>, prevent the submit, set <code>error-message</code> (for example from <code>result.message</code>) and <code>is-invalid</code> on the group, and move focus to the first radio in the group. Clear them when the user makes a choice. See the <a href="/docs/concepts/validation#whole-form-validation-on-submit">whole-form validation pattern</a>.</li>
<li>Use radios only for genuinely mutually-exclusive choices among a small, fixed set (roughly two to seven options). For a single instantly-applied on/off setting, use <code>aegov-toggle</code> instead; for longer option lists, use <code>aegov-select</code>.</li>
<li>Check colour contrast for any custom <code>extra-class</code> background or text colour against your chosen <code>variant</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="additional-notes">Additional notes</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>size</code> on both components accepts a responsive breakpoint string, the same convention used by Badge, Banner, and Checkbox (e.g. <code>size="sm md:base"</code>).</li>
<li><code>appearance</code> on <code>aegov-radio</code> is written by its parent group and shouldn't be set directly — set <code>appearance</code> on the <code>aegov-radio-group</code> instead. A standalone radio with no parent group always renders <code>default</code>.</li>
<li><code>name</code>/form submission are handled via <code>ElementInternals</code> on the host element, not the inner shadow-DOM <code><input></code> — reading <code>radio.name</code> or checking form data works exactly like a native input. The shadow DOM's own <code><input></code> also carries the name (so a required radio can report <code>valueMissing</code>), but it never submits anything itself. See the note on keyboard support below for why it matters more here than it does for <code>aegov-checkbox</code>.</li>
<li>Because each radio's inner native <code><input></code> lives in its own shadow root, the inputs never form a group with each other even when their names match, so the browser has no native "radio button group" to apply its own keyboard behaviour to. <code>aegov-radio-group</code> reimplements mutual exclusivity, the single tab stop and arrow-key navigation in JS instead. See Keyboard support for the resulting behaviour.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Tab</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus into the group, landing on the selected radio — or the first enabled radio if none is selected. The group is a single tab stop; the next <kbd>Tab</kbd> leaves it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus out of the group. Entering the group backwards with nothing selected lands on the last enabled radio, as native radios do.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus to the next enabled radio and selects it, wrapping from the last option to the first. In RTL, <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> moves forward instead of <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus to the previous enabled radio and selects it, wrapping from the first option to the last. In RTL, <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> moves back instead of <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Space</kbd></td>
<td>Selects the focused radio and deselects any other radio checked within the same group.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<p>Arrow keys move focus <strong>and</strong> change the selection, matching native radios and the WAI-ARIA <code>radiogroup</code> pattern. Disabled radios are skipped. Because moving through the options selects each one, don't trigger consequential side effects on <code>aegovRadioGroupChange</code>.</p>

</div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-textarea</code> renders a real native <code><textarea></code>, optionally wrapped alongside a copy button (when read-only and copyable) and a character counter (when <code>maxlength</code> is set), with hint and error regions as siblings.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/textarea/textarea-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a textarea"></p>

<p>Wrap the field in <code>aegov-form-field</code> and set <code>is-invalid="true"</code> together with <code>error-message</code> there — the form field cascades both <code>is-invalid</code> and the error text down to the textarea, which renders the actual error region and wires it up via <code>aria-describedby</code>.                     <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Renders a real native <code><textarea></code>, so keyboard editing, selection, autofill, spellcheck, and assistive-technology behaviour all come for free.</li>
<li>The label reaches the native <code><textarea></code> inside the shadow DOM. ID references can't cross that boundary on their own, so the component resolves each naming source to text and gives it to the inner textarea: <code>aegov-label</code> inside <code>aegov-form-field</code>, an <code>aegov-label for="…"</code> pointing at the host's <code>id</code> or <code>field-id</code>, a native <code><label for="…"></code> pointing at the host's <code>id</code>, and <code>aria-label</code> / <code>aria-labelledby</code> set on the host.</li>
<li>An <code>aria-describedby</code> you set on the host is handled the same way: the referenced text becomes part of the textarea's description, read before the component's own counter, error and hint.</li>
<li><code>is-required</code> sets the native <code>required</code> attribute, exposing the requirement to assistive technology automatically.</li>
<li>Setting <code>maxlength</code> applies the real native <code>maxlength</code> attribute (a genuine, browser-enforced typing limit, not just a visual cue) alongside the live counter. The visible "11 / 20" count is hidden from assistive technology; instead the field's description includes the remaining count in words ("9 characters remaining"), and a polite status announces it about a second after typing pauses, rather than on every keystroke.</li>
<li>The copy button (when <code>is-copyable</code> + <code>is-readonly</code>) is a real, keyboard-reachable <code><button></code> — <code>Tab</code> moves to it right after the textarea — with a bilingual <code>aria-label</code> ("Copy to clipboard" / "نسخ إلى الحافظة"). The button keeps its name after use; a visually hidden <code>role="status"</code> region announces "Copied" / "تم النسخ" instead. No developer translation is needed.</li>
<li>The error region only takes <code>role="alert"</code> after the user has blurred the field at least once, the form has reported it invalid, or <code>validate('submit')</code> has run, so a validation message present at initial load isn't announced as an interruption.</li>
<li>The <code>hint</code> / <code>error-message</code> props (or the <code>hint</code> / <code>error</code> slots placed inside <code>aegov-textarea</code>) are linked to the textarea's description automatically, and the hint stays visible while an error shows. When the textarea is wrapped in <code>aegov-form-field</code>, an element in the form field's own <code>hint</code> slot is linked too; other text placed beside the textarea is not.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibility">Developer responsibility</h3>
<p>The following is required for a developer to add additionally or pay attention to regarding this component.</p>
<ul>
<li>Always provide a visible label — <code>aegov-label</code> inside <code>aegov-form-field</code> is the preferred pattern. For a standalone textarea with no visible label, set <code>aria-label</code> on the host directly.</li>
<li>If the textarea collects the user's own details (for example a postal address), set the matching <code>autocomplete</code> value such as <code>autocomplete="street-address"</code> so the browser can fill it in (WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose). The attribute is passed through to the native textarea.</li>
<li>Pick a sensible <code>maxlength</code>: too low frustrates users mid-sentence, too high makes the counter meaningless. 500–1000 characters suits most feedback-style fields.</li>
<li>Confirm a copyable field's content is genuinely safe to land in a user's clipboard history before enabling <code>is-copyable</code>.</li>
<li>Handle form submission yourself. When the browser blocks a submit (for example a required field is empty), it only shows its own temporary bubble, in the browser's language: the field gets no error text on the page and no <code>aria-invalid</code>. Use the <a href="/docs/concepts/validation#whole-form-validation-on-submit">whole-form validation pattern</a>: on submit, call <code>validate('submit')</code> on each field and set <code>is-invalid</code> and <code>error-message</code> from the result, so every error is shown, announced and stays on screen.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="additional-notes">Additional notes</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>size</code> accepts a responsive breakpoint string, the same convention used by Badge, Banner, and Checkbox (e.g. <code>size="sm md:base"</code>).</li>
<li><code>is-copyable</code> silently has no effect unless <code>is-readonly</code> is also set — there's no copy button on an editable field, by design.</li>
<li>The character counter only ever shows an "over limit" state when <code>value</code> is set to something longer than <code>maxlength</code> <em>programmatically</em> — ordinary typing can never exceed it, since the native <code>maxlength</code> attribute blocks further input at the browser level.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Tab</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus into the textarea. When a copy button is present, one more <code>Tab</code> reaches it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd></td>
<td>Moves focus to the previous focusable element.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Enter</kbd></td>
<td>Inserts a new line inside the textarea — never submits an enclosing form.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> <em>(on the copy button)</em></td>
<td>Copies the textarea's value to the clipboard.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Standard text-editing shortcuts</td>
<td>All native browser behaviour applies — selection, cursor movement, cut/copy/paste.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p>The <code>aegov-accordion</code> component composes a wrapper with one or more <code>aegov-accordion-item</code> children. The parent owns shared configuration — icon style, heading size, single-open vs. multi-open behaviour, and first/last positioning — and propagates it to each item automatically.</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/accordion/accordion-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of an accordion"></p>

                <section class="article-section">
                    <h2 class="text-h4 lg:text-h3 xl:text-h2 mb-4 tracking-tight text-primary-700" id="notes">Notes</h2>
                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Each trigger renders as a real <code><button></code> with <code>aria-expanded</code> reflecting the open state and <code>aria-controls</code> linked to its panel.</li>
<li>Each panel uses <code>role="region"</code> and <code>aria-labelledby</code> pointing at its trigger, so screen readers announce the heading–content relationship.</li>
<li><code>Enter</code> and <code>Space</code> toggle the focused item — free, native <code><button></code> behaviour, no custom key handling needed.</li>
<li>Arrow-key navigation (<code>ArrowUp</code> / <code>ArrowDown</code> / <code>Home</code> / <code>End</code>) moves focus between item triggers within the same accordion, matching the <a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/">WAI-ARIA Accordion pattern</a>. A nested accordion's own triggers are handled by its own keydown listener and does not interfere with the parent's.</li>
<li>Collapsed panels get the HTML <code>inert</code> attribute on their content wrapper. This removes every focusable descendant — buttons, links, inputs — from both the tab order and the accessibility tree in one step, so there is no focus leaking into hidden content.</li>
<li>Disabled items set <code>aria-disabled="true"</code> on the trigger (never the native <code>disabled</code> attribute) and do not emit a toggle event when activated, but the trigger stays focusable.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibility">Developer responsibility</h3>
<p>The following is required for a developer to add additionally or pay attention to regarding this component.</p>
<ul>
<li>Provide a meaningful <code>heading</code> (or <code>accordion-item-heading</code> slot) on every item — without it the trigger announces to screen readers as just "button".</li>
<li>When using <code>default-open</code>, make sure the index actually points at a real child item.</li>
<li><code>aegov-accordion-item</code> must always be used inside <code>aegov-accordion</code>. Using it standalone logs a console error and its toggle behaviour will not be wired up by any parent.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="additional-notes">Additional notes</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>aegovAccordionItemToggle</code> is dispatched with <code>bubbles: true</code> (verified against the compiled component — <code>createEvent(this, "aegovAccordionItemToggle", 7)</code>, where flag <code>7</code> sets <code>bubbles</code>, <code>composed</code>, and <code>cancelable</code> all <code>true</code>) — but in practice it never reaches a bubble-phase listener on the parent <code>aegov-accordion</code> or beyond, because the parent's own internal listener (attached directly on each item to sync <code>isOpen</code>) calls <code>stopPropagation()</code>. Attach your listener to each <code>aegov-accordion-item</code> directly, or use a capture-phase listener on an ancestor if you need a single listener.</li>
<li><code>heading-level</code> cascades from parent to children automatically, and auto-increments by 1 for an accordion nested inside another accordion's item — so a nested accordion's triggers render one heading level deeper by default, keeping the outline correct without extra configuration.</li>
<li>Focusable controls nested inside a collapsed panel are automatically excluded from the tab order via <code>inert</code>. You do not need to manually disable or hide them.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Action</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Toggle the focused accordion item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowDown</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next accordion trigger.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ArrowUp</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the previous accordion trigger.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Home</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the first accordion trigger.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>End</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the last accordion trigger.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next focusable element on the page.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the previous focusable element on the page.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="introduction">Introduction</h2>
<p><code>aegov-header</code> is the standard top-of-page header for UAE Federal Government websites. It ties the page to the official government identity — the top bar, the "Learn more" verification panel and, for authorities, the UAE emblem — and carries the site's logo and primary navigation.</p>
<p>You configure it in two ways:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Attributes</strong> set <em>how</em> the header behaves: who the entity is, which variant, where the navigation collapses, whether it sticks.</li>
<li><strong>Slots</strong> decide <em>what content</em> goes <em>where</em>: you add your own elements with a <code>slot="…"</code> attribute, and the header places them in the right region.</li>
</ul>
<p>Only <code>entity-name</code> and <code>entity-domain</code> are required. With just those two, you already get the full official top bar.</p>

</div>

    <h2 id="attributes">Attributes</h2>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Attribute</th>
<th>What it does</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>entity-name</code>, <code>entity-domain</code></td>
<td><strong>Required.</strong> Who the entity is. Used in the "Learn more" panel; <code>entity-domain</code> is also where the logo links to. If either is missing, the top bar shows an inline error so the mistake is obvious during development.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>variant</code></td>
<td><code>ministry</code> (default) for federal ministries — the end of the logo row holds your <code>search</code> slot. <code>authority</code> for authorities, councils and regulators — the UAE emblem takes that place instead.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>emblem-color</code></td>
<td>Colour of the UAE emblem on the <code>authority</code> variant: <code>aeblack</code> (default), <code>whitely</code> or <code>aegold</code>. See <strong>Emblem colour</strong> below.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>collapse-at</code></td>
<td>Where the navigation row gives way to the menu button: <code>md</code> (768px), <code>lg</code> (1024px, default), <code>xl</code> (1280px) or <code>2xl</code> (1536px). Pick a later breakpoint if your navigation is long — around five items fit at <code>lg</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>skip-content-container</code></td>
<td>Adds a "Skip to content" link pointing at your main content — set it on every page. Takes the element's ID (<code>#main</code> or <code>main</code>), not a CSS selector.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>logo-label</code></td>
<td>Accessible name for the logo link.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>gsr-stars</code></td>
<td>Shows your entity's Global Star Rating System for Services badge next to the logo: <code>1</code> to <code>5</code> stars, or <code>0</code> (default) for no badge. See <strong>Global Star Rating badge</strong> below.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>is-sticky</code></td>
<td>Keeps the navigation row pinned to the top while scrolling, from <code>collapse-at</code> up; the top bar and logo row scroll away. It stops working if any ancestor has <code>overflow: hidden</code>, <code>auto</code> or <code>scroll</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>drawer-size</code>, <code>label-menu</code>, <code>label-menu-close</code></td>
<td>Fine-tune the menu drawer's width and its accessible names. The labels already default to English or Arabic, so you rarely need them.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<p>The full list with types and defaults is in the <strong>API reference</strong> tab.</p>
<h3 id="emblem-colour">Emblem colour</h3>
<p>On the <code>authority</code> variant, <code>emblem-color</code> sets the colour of the UAE emblem at the end of the logo row. The emblem is an official mark, so it takes one of three palette colours only:</p>

<tr>
<th>Value</th>
<th>Use it when</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>aeblack</code> (default)</td>
<td>The header sits on a light background.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>whitely</code></td>
<td>The header sits on a dark background, for example in dark mode.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>aegold</code></td>
<td>Your entity shows the emblem in gold.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

On the <code>ministry</code> variant the attribute is ignored.</p>
<h3 id="global-star-rating-badge">Global Star Rating badge</h3>
<p>If your entity holds a rating in the Global Star Rating System for Services, set <code>gsr-stars</code> to its number of stars, from <code>1</code> to <code>5</code>. The header shows the official badge right after the logo. Leave it out, or set <code>0</code>, and no badge appears. Available from version 4.0.3.</p>

<li><strong>It sits beside the logo, not inside its link.</strong> The badge is vertically centred on the logo and moves to the logo's left on Arabic (RTL) pages. It stays visible at every screen size.</li>
<li><strong>It matches your logo's size.</strong> The badge takes the logo's height, kept between 50px and 80px, so it never towers over a small logo or shrinks to unreadable. Don't size it yourself.</li>
<li><strong>The artwork is built in.</strong> Don't add your own badge image — the header draws the official one for 1 to 5 stars.</li>
<li><strong>It costs nothing when unused.</strong> The artwork (about 14KB) loads only when <code>gsr-stars</code> is above <code>0</code>, and its space is reserved before it arrives, so the page doesn't jump.</li>

    <h2 id="slots">Slots</h2>
<p>Add a <code>slot="…"</code> attribute to any element inside <code>aegov-header</code>, and the header moves it to that region. <strong>The order you write the slots in doesn't matter</strong> — the slot name decides where content appears.</p>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Slot</th>
<th>Where it appears</th>
<th>Visible</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>actions</code></td>
<td>Official top bar, at the end</td>
<td>Always</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>logo</code></td>
<td>Logo row, at the start</td>
<td>Always</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>search</code></td>
<td>Logo row, at the end (<code>ministry</code> only)</td>
<td>From <code>collapse-at</code> up</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>navigation</code></td>
<td>Navigation row, at the start</td>
<td>From <code>collapse-at</code> up</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>secondary-actions</code></td>
<td>Navigation row, at the end</td>
<td>From <code>collapse-at</code> up</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>mobile-content</code></td>
<td>Inside the menu drawer</td>
<td>Below <code>collapse-at</code>, when opened</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<p>Two rules make the header work on every screen size:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Repeat your navigation in <code>mobile-content</code>.</strong> A slot's content can only appear in one place, so the drawer can't reuse the <code>navigation</code> slot. Copy the links in — and anything essential from <code>search</code> or <code>secondary-actions</code>. If <code>mobile-content</code> is empty, the menu button opens an empty drawer.</li>
<li><strong>Let the navigation own its landmark.</strong> <code>aegov-navbar</code> renders its own <code><nav></code> (named with <code>label-nav</code>), so don't wrap it in another one. If you use plain links instead, wrap them in your own <code><nav aria-label="…"></code>.</li>
</ol>

</div>

<li><strong>The item stays a link.</strong> Clicking "Services" still goes to <code>/services</code>; the dropdown is an extra layer, not a replacement.</li>
<li><strong><code>trigger="hover"</code> still works from the keyboard.</strong> The navbar item adds a chevron button that opens the dropdown with <code>Enter</code> or <code>Space</code>, and <code>Tab</code> moves through the links inside.</li>
<li><strong>Give the panel a width class</strong> such as <code>w-64</code>. A dropdown can hold anything — a simple link list as in the example, or several columns with headings for a larger menu.</li>
<li><strong>Keep the main destination on the item.</strong> Every dropdown in the example sits on an item that still has its own <code>href</code>.</li>

<p>Add an icon to a navbar item with <code>slot="icon-start"</code> on the <code>svg</code>, as on "Home" in the example.</p>
<h2 id="secondary-actions-with-tooltips">Secondary actions with tooltips</h2>
<p>The <code>secondary-actions</code> slot holds the compact actions at the end of the navigation row — in the example: search, sign in, U.ASK AI and a dark-mode switch. Wrap them in one <code>div</code> with <code>slot="secondary-actions"</code>. Each is an icon-only <code>aegov-button</code> (<code>is-icon="true"</code>, <code>appearance="link"</code>) with an <code>aria-label</code> for screen readers, wrapped in an <code>aegov-tooltip</code> that shows the same label on hover and focus.</p>
<p>Like the navigation, this row is hidden below <code>collapse-at</code> — so put the same actions in <code>mobile-content</code>.</p>

    <h2 id="rtl-support">RTL support</h2>
<p>The header reads the direction from the closest <code>dir</code> ancestor or the <code>html</code> element, and updates if it changes. In RTL, the layout mirrors (logo on the right with the star rating badge to its left, drawer sliding in from the left) and the default menu labels and the badge's text alternative switch to Arabic.                     <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable to this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Renders the page's <code>banner</code> landmark, with the official top bar inside it.</li>
<li>The "Learn more" trigger has <code>aria-expanded</code> and <code>aria-controls</code>; <code>Escape</code> closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger.</li>
<li>The menu button has <code>aria-expanded</code> and <code>aria-controls</code> pointing at the drawer. Opening the drawer moves focus into it and traps <code>Tab</code> inside; closing it (button, <code>Escape</code> or backdrop) returns focus to the menu button.</li>
<li>Growing the viewport past <code>collapse-at</code> closes an open drawer, so the same links are never reachable twice.</li>
<li>With <code>skip-content-container</code>, a "Skip to content" link becomes the first focusable element on the page.</li>
<li>With <code>gsr-stars</code>, the star rating badge is an image outside the logo link whose text alternative states the rating — "Global Star Rating System for Services: 4 stars" in English, "<span lang="ar" dir="rtl">نظام النجوم العالمي لتصنيف الخدمات: 4 نجوم</span>" in Arabic.</li>
<li>Built-in text switches between English and Arabic based on direction: the menu labels and the star rating badge's text follow the closest <code>dir</code> ancestor or <code>html</code>; the top bar text ("Learn more", the panel) and "Skip to content" follow <code>dir</code> on <code>html</code> only.</li>
<li>Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Use exactly one <code>aegov-header</code> per page, at the start of the <code>body</code>.</li>
<li>Give the logo an accessible name — <code>alt</code> on the image and/or <code>logo-label</code>.</li>
<li>Give the <code>navigation</code> content its own <code><nav></code> landmark with a name (<code>aegov-navbar</code> does this with <code>label-nav</code>), and give the drawer's copy a different name.</li>
<li>Fill <code>mobile-content</code> whenever the menu button can appear; the component warns in the console when it is empty.</li>
<li>Give icon-only buttons in <code>search</code> and <code>secondary-actions</code> an <code>aria-label</code>.</li>
<li>Set <code>lang</code> and <code>dir</code> on the <code>html</code> element for Arabic pages, and mark the language link with <code>lang="ar"</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Action</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code> / <code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Move between focusable elements. Trapped inside the menu drawer while it is open.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code> / <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Activate the focused control — menu button, "Learn more", close button, or a link.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Escape</code></td>
<td>Close the menu drawer or the "Learn more" panel, returning focus to its trigger.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

    <h2 id="anatomy">Anatomy</h2>
<p><code>aegov-pagination</code> renders a single <code><nav></code> landmark wrapping a <code><ul></code> of buttons: Previous, an optional First before it and Last after Next, page-number buttons with ellipsis tokens between distant ranges (or, in <code>compact</code> mode, a plain "page X of Y" text indicator instead of page numbers).</p>
<p><img src="https://designsystem.gov.ae/storage/documentation/pagination/pagination-anatomoy-img-001.png" alt="Image showing anatomy of a pagination control"></p>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Item</th>
<th>Name</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td><strong>Nav landmark</strong></td>
<td>The <code><nav></code> element, labelled "Pagination"</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>2</code></td>
<td><strong>Previous / Next</strong></td>
<td>Always rendered; disabled at the first/last page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td><strong>First / Last</strong></td>
<td>Optional, shown only when <code>is-enabled-first-last</code> is set</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>4</code></td>
<td><strong>Page button</strong></td>
<td>One per visible page number; the active one carries <code>aria-current="page"</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>5</code></td>
<td><strong>Ellipsis</strong></td>
<td>Decorative, marks a collapsed range of hidden page numbers</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

                    <div class="prose max-w-none prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:text-aeblack-800 prose-a:text-primary-700 prose-h1:text-h3 lg:prose-h1:text-h2 xl:prose-h1:text-h1 prose-h2:text-h4 lg:prose-h2:text-h3 xl:prose-h2:text-h2 prose-h3:text-h5 lg:prose-h3:text-h4 xl:prose-h3:text-h3 prose-h4:text-h6 lg:prose-h4:text-h5 xl:prose-h4:text-h4 prose-h5:text-lg lg:prose-h5:text-h6 xl:prose-h5:text-h5 prose-h6:text-base lg:prose-h6:text-lg xl:prose-h6:text-h6">
    <p>The following notes are applicable of this component.</p>
<h3 id="built-in-accessibility">Built-in accessibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Renders as a <code><nav></code> landmark with <code>aria-label="Pagination"</code> (Arabic: "ترقيم الصفحات") so screen readers announce it among page landmarks.</li>
<li>The active page button carries <code>aria-current="page"</code> and a descriptive <code>aria-label</code> such as "Page 3, current page" (Arabic: "الصفحة 3، الصفحة الحالية").</li>
<li>Previous, Next, First, and Last buttons are named by their visible text: the built-in bilingual label ("Previous", "Next", "First", "Last"; Arabic "السابق", "التالي", "الأول", "الأخير" when <code>dir="rtl"</code> is detected) or your <code>label-*</code> value. Their chevron icons are <code>aria-hidden</code>.</li>
<li>The compact variant's position indicator ("Page 3 of 10" / "الصفحة 3 من 10") sits in a polite <code>aria-live</code> region, announced whenever the page changes.</li>
<li>Disabled buttons set both the native <code>disabled</code> attribute and <code>aria-disabled="true"</code>.</li>
<li>Ellipsis tokens are <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> — decorative only, never announced.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="developer-responsibilities">Developer responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Always update <code>page-current</code> in response to <code>aegovPaginationPageChange</code> — the component never updates its own state; without the update, clicking does nothing.</li>
<li>After a page change, move focus to (or scroll to) the updated content region so keyboard users don't lose their place — the button just activated may become disabled (e.g. Next on the last page) and drop focus.</li>
<li>In the <code>default</code> variant there is no live region, so announce the new result range yourself (e.g. an <code>aria-live="polite"</code> summary next to the results).</li>
<li>Prefer <code>compact</code> on narrow viewports rather than letting page-number buttons wrap onto a second line.</li>
<li>Enable <code>is-enabled-first-last</code> on lists beyond roughly 50 pages, so users can reach either end without repeatedly clicking Next.</li>
<li><code>label-*</code> props set both the visible text and the accessible name, so voice-control users can say what they see (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.3 Label in Name). Keep custom labels short and clear, e.g. "Previous page".</li>
<li>Never hide <code>.pagination__nav-label</code> with <code>display: none</code> or <code>visibility: hidden</code>: that text is the button's only name. To show just the chevrons on small screens, hide the text visually (a screen-reader-only style) so it is still read out.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="keyboard-support">Keyboard support</h3>
<div class="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-aeblack-950/10" data-table-wrap=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Action</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the next pagination button. Disabled buttons are skipped.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Shift + Tab</code></td>
<td>Move focus to the previous pagination button.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Enter</code>, <code>Space</code></td>
<td>Activate the focused button.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<h3 id="notes-2">Notes</h3>
<ul>
<li>An unrecognised <code>variant</code> falls back to <code>default</code> and logs a console warning in development builds only; an unrecognised <code>size</code> token falls back to <code>base</code> silently.</li>
<li>Setting <code>count-sibling</code>/<code>count-boundary</code> high enough that every page number always fits removes the ellipsis entirely — this is expected, not a bug: the algorithm only collapses a range when doing so would hide two or more page numbers.</li>
</ul>
